title: Amazing, I'll never go back to paste again.
text:
This stuff is super easy to use. You'll see people complaining about it being slippery and hard to hold in place ... I had to install this under a desk on my home server, which means I could not lay the case flat. (The Corsair H100i V2 pump died and I was replacing it with an H100i Pro). So I put two tiny daubs of regular paste in the top corners of the processor and stuck it on with that. Then I put everything together and fired up the system.

I had been using Thermal Grizzly Conductonaut liquid metal before this. It had dried out and failed after two years. It's a serious pain to install and it is really, really hard to get applied correctly. It's almost worse to try to clean it off. I used a Dremel and a buffing wheel and polished it off after getting the bulk removed with ArticClean binary cleaner. I'll never use that stuff again. BUT it did do a good job as a new install until it began failing. The problem is that eventually either your cooling solution or your thermal paste is going to fail and then you're going to be taking things apart ...

Degrading thermal paste, even liquid metals, is a serious problem for high use, high availability, high performance, long duration computer systems. I have replaced the thermal paste on the processor for this machine at least a half dozen times because I've had at least a half dozen CPU coolers on this machine.

The computer I'm using this pad on is an AMD FX 8350 Black (On an ASUS 990FX Sabertooth R1 board) that's been running this machine for over ten years. Pretty much everything on the machine has been replaced multiple times except for the processor and motherboard. The processor has a nearly 25% overclock running 24/7/365 (4.95 GHz) It serves all my multimedia (which is a LOT) and is my security camera server (22 cameras), plus the computer I use (3 video cards, six monitors) at the main desk in my shop/office/man cave. Because of the camera system, "idle" is never less than around 50% CPU clock cycles. I can and do use it for gaming though I'm not much of a gamer. It's not a gaming computer. Think more along the lines of a semi-truck than a sports car. It works hard. It gets hot. It's still doing a great job after all this time and I have no intention of replacing it one second before I have to.

This is VERY impressive performance for a computer. I don't know if I got lucky with processor and board or it's just that this combination is particularly robust. Whatever the reason, it has been and continues to be a truly great machine.

I don't want to trust the cooling system to just any old nonsense. That's why I tried Thermal Grizzly liquid metal last time. I thought long and hard about using this pad before buying and installing it. I'm really glad I did. My temps are almost exactly even with what I got with the liquid metal even though this pad is only rated for half the thermal conductivity that the liquid metal is. So the conclusion I've come to is that the liquid metal either wasn't applied optimally, it squeezed out to the edges when the cold plate on the pump was attached or some other unseeable and unknowable problem occurred ... OR both thermal conductors have maxed out the capacity of my cooling solution. It would not be at all surprising as difficult as that stuff is to apply on a vertical surface that there was an unseen problem in the installation.

The pad was super easy. I just put a tiny little daub of TX-2 (that I had laying around, nothing special as far as pastes go) on the top corners of the CPU to hold the pad in place while I bolted on the pump. Those two tiny bits of paste are well away from the die and should in no way interfere with the heat carrying capacity of the system. I literally used paste to paste the pad on long enough to finish the installation.

It should be noted that I bought the 40x40mm pad which covered the entire lid and that my CPU is obviously not delidded. I think that's important because it establishes maximum conductivity across the largest possible area. It's only $3 more for the larger pad, don't cheap out on this. Be sure to measure your CPU, look up the dimensional specs or just buy the larger pad and be prepared to cut it down.

I also polished the CPU and cold plate with a Dremel and a buffing wheel using green rouge. I had to do that to the CPU to get all the liquid metal off so I figured I might as well do the cold plate while I was at it. I didn't lap it, I didn't mate the surfaces perfectly, I just put a semi-mirror polish on the surfaces free handed. Be careful if you do that so as not to create micro-concave areas that will cause problems with gapping.

Temperatures are running around 40 degrees normal use (remember I said it never actually goes to "idle" in normal use?) to around 50 under max load and I don't stress test it with Prime95 or anything like that. There's no need to stress test it, all I care about are real-world results and it's under stress just because it's on. When I turn everything off and it is truly idle it sits just a couple degrees F (~24C) above ambient.

As mentioned previously, this pad is rated about half the thermal conductivity of the Thermal Grizzly Conductonaut liquid metal it replaced and it does as well or slightly better on my machine. That could mean that both the Thermal Grizzly liquid metal and this pad are maxing out the possible conduction of heat between my CPU and the pump cold plate. This pad is rated for thermal conductivity about four times what MX-4 produces. There are other factors besides thermal conductivity that work together in determining the effectiveness of your cooling solution. If you're not getting as good or better results with this than you did with MX-4, you're doing something wrong and/or one of those other factors needs to be addressed. The incontrovertible proof of that is all the other highly positive reviews. If we're all getting excellent results and you're not, it is very likely something on your end that is the problem and not an issue with this pad. Unlike paste that can have unknown and unseen air gaps, bubbles, uneven spreading etc. this pad is either in place on clean surfaces or it is not. This isn't arbitrary. The physics of this mean that if it works for me, it works the same for you. If it doesn't work for you as well or better than MX-4 or a similar thermal conduction paste then it's a problem that YOU have, not a problem with this pad.

I'm not saying people who have issues with this pad don't know what they're doing. I'm merely pointing out the irrefutable logic of the physical science involved. If all the pads are the same (meaning no manufacturing defects) and every installation follows the same basic process on the same basic materials ... (CPU heat spreader/lid > thermal conductor > copper cold plate) And the vast majority of installations are extremely successful but yours isn't -- Then it's not the pad. You need to find that other variable that's causing the problem if you want to get the same positive results the rest of us are getting. It's worth the effort because this pad is an amazing and highly effective solution. I've been building computers for almost 30 years so it's not like I'm a novice at this stuff, but if you want to challenge my logic please feel free to comment and we'll discuss it.

SO -- The performance of this thermal pad is phenomenal. I'm very, very happy with it and the fact that it will outlast my water cooler is a big plus. (I now have three water cooler radiators laying around so I may just go to a reservoir fed open liquid system next time, and I can use this pad again if I do.) Time will tell if it actually resists the degradation that thermal paste experiences and if it dies like thermal paste I'll come back and amend this review. If you don't see an edit below then it's still doing a great job and that being the case ... I'll never go back to goop again.

28 December 2020 - Two years later and the pad is still performing like the day I installed it. I have to shut down the machine and clean the radiator about twice a year but that's it. With a clean radiator on the overclocked processor previously mentioned this pad still works like brand new.

title: Solid and Flexible Business Desktop Replacement
text:
Adding my review because many here are focused on gaming. I do not game, but use some intensive graphics and demanding programs for work. I tried a slightly less expensive solution (Asus X750JB) as a mobile desktop but was dissatisfied and went with this machine as an upgrade.

It solved two of three dissatisfactions from the lesser ASUS, namely having a backlit keyboard and reliable graphics (the previous 740M failed me). The third is Windows 8, and I am stuck with that, but had learned on the ASUS to live with the excellent Start8 interface.

Went on to add an mSATA SSD boot drive, and the migration was a terrible headache despite installing SSDs successfully four other times. The UEFI standard and Windows Boot Manager is to blame for the difficulties. Ultimately, got it working with 6 hours lost. I did notice that the stock 7200 drive gave a faster boot than the ASUS 5400, but compared to an SSD, it's really nothing. There are 2 mSATA expansion slots, a treat, and the 7200 remains.

Now my GE70 SSD machine blazes almost as fast as my hand built power PC tower. Because I do not game and am not currently overclocking, have not seen the extreme temperatures referenced in lower ratings. The display is very nice, rich and detailed, and I have no problem running dual 1080 monitors and/or the screen with an additional monitor. This machine advertises running three displays and no trouble believing that, but I was shooting for and found ultimate reliability on two (again the 740M in the ASUS crash-froze on me repeatedly).

The Steel Series keyboard has a better feel, response and reach compared to the ASUS, nice legible characters on keys, but the windows key is annoyingly on the right side and the often-used Delete and Alt keys are a misplaced and still having problems adjusting to both after 15 hours of use. Touch pad is standard as any other.

I suspect gamers might find this laptop very understated, it is not stylish by any measure and the glossy hard plastic top shows every smudge and has me concerned about scratches and even breaks; moreover, it has a sharp plastic edge seam. As a business desktop replacement I do not mind the understated nature... looks like an engineer's machine really.

Other plusses: this laptop is very light in weight for its specs, having opened the machine, it appears good quality components are in place here, arrived with a useable $1 dust slip cover which is more than I can say about many other laptops. Bloatware was typical and manageable. 12Gb is excessive but allows me to comfortably dedicate 4Gb to Ubuntu VM.

Other minuses: the battery life is pitiful, but I do not use the laptop on battery for any length of time, so not concerned. The BIOS is not great, seems perhaps it's interface was not created with English as a first language and BIOS update not as clean as other new generation machines.

Verdict: I found the laptop I was looking for. With the SSD ($79), the total package is a bit more expensive for what you get, and there are apparently many competitors in this range. MSI does not tout it's display enough, but it should, this is a top notch quality 17.3" display. If the machine remains reliable, I will be satisfied.

text:
First time using a GMRS system and this was exactly what I needed for how I'm using it. My off-road group has switched from CB to GMRS and this was the model I went with to make sure we could all keep comms up. With no modifications or aftermarket purchases, I was able to keep up 2-way comms with vehicles out to at least 2 miles away from inside my Jeep (never got further than that). It was all very clear transmissions and having the 2 button PTT option was nice for a private conversation to one other driver.

I can't speak to the battery too much but having it on and using it 2 days in a row, while keeping it off during the night, I never showed less than the 3/3 bars on the battery. That was even after resting it at night in below freezing temps. Very impressed with the life so I don't have to carry a separate charger or extra battery.

Setup for basic usage was very easy although getting into more advanced functions is fairly complex. Being able to switch between channel and ferq mode is simple, just turn it on/off while holding a single button. Also, I like that you can turn on high power with a single button push. Anything more than those adjustments and setting a frequency is complex however. Its possible to access the menu on the unit but its really to small to display a lot of text so you need the manual in front of you to really be able to make any useful changes. Not a huge issue for me as I don't need to do much more than set a channel and go, but for those that want to really dive into how the unit operates, its going to be somewhat of a chore.

Overall highly recommend the unit for anyone wheeling in a group that needs a simple comms setup and doesn't want to deal with mounting a more permeant unit. Don't forget to get your callsign to stay legal!

title: Worst camera we've ever owned.
text:
Stars: 1 of 5 . (is 0 an option?)

Let me ask you one question: Would you want to purchase a camera from a company that would design a rotating camera that has its reset button under a flap that's normally INSIDE the machine unless it's rotated to an extreme angle? Because that's the design choice this company made, and the first time I reset the camera it tried to turn before I had a chance to close the memory-card door. Luckily the motor is too weak to break the door or strip the gears inside. Seriously the reset procedure exposes your device to the possibility of damage!

Did I mention that the docs that came with it do not say where the MicroSD card actually goes? Or that their site says there's a bit of Mac software for download that doesn't appear to exist? Or that the website says the reset button FOR THAT SPECIFIC MODEL is on the back, but it's not there! Seriously, I took the darn thing apart hoping to find that the reset button was on the circuit board. It's not there either. Wanna know where it is? It's next to the memory card slot, you have to turn the camera so it's looking straight up to reveal it. I could NOT find this on their site or in the included documentation anywhere!

I'd also like to mention that I have no idea what the default credentials are. The site says it's admin/12345. It's not. I thought maybe I had gotten .a refurbed one or something, thus leading me down the path towards doing a complete reset. I *did* a complete reset, several times, and that username password (and a number of variations) did not work. Basically without this username and password it's like having a fancy Digital SLR and only having the automatic settings available. It can serve SOME uses but I cannot, for example, use the Motion Detection because the default setting is far too sensitive. I need the username/password to change the motion detection sensitivity... yet I don't need it to actually watch a video stream or to get the endless barrage of alerts from said sensitivity. Umm.. from a product design point of view, I *really* don't understand that.

This camera's going back, I just don't have the time to dink around with this when there are so many other cameras on the market. To LaView I have this to say: Sort out your software, sort out your website. I can forgive a software oversight or two but this whole fiasco ate up a perfectly fine evening and this level of incompetence has really soured me on your entire brand.

I installed  Linux Mint on the 256gb internal SSD in a dual boot configuration beside the Windows 10 OS that it came with. Instead it goes into "Hibernation" and locks it's partition and/or drive.  So the Linux installation can't proceed properly until you go into Windows and disable the hibernation 'feature'.  You do this by opening up a Windows command prompt in Administrator mode and typing in the "powercfg -h off"  command.  I hope I remembered the  command syntax correctly, if you get an error, just google it. So, anyway, it's perfectly compatible with Linux Mate 18.3.  And likely most other Linux distros as well. title: The RAM worked without errors.
text:
Unlike DDR4, there's really not a lot to say about DDR3. Either it works or it doesn't. Use Memtest86+ to test DDR2 and DDR3. Version 5.31b is the "latest" version. It hasn't been updated in a LONG time, but that's OK because DDR2/DDR3 is fairly old RAM. Run 2 passes for an initial test. Most all RAM with any problems will fail that 2 pass test (2nd pass is longer/more thorough then the 1st). Then later, run an overnight or at least 6 hour test.

The RAM DIMMs I greatly prefer for DDR2 or DDR3 is either Samsung OR Hynix/SKHynix. Of course, whenever possible, use matched RAM. Unmatched RAM can work, but is more of a crapshoot. Never mix RAM of different ranks = never mix single rank RAM with dual rank (etc.) RAM.

title: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base - No Roku Sound
text:
I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.

text:
The camera is OK. It is very easy to set up and use, including online access. The night vision works pretty well. Image quality is decent, though the resolution is too low for modern equipment. MyDlink is a plus in my opinion - setup is pretty easy and you don't need to open ports in your router/firewall. You don't have to be a tech expert to set this up.

The resolution is unbelievably low. I didn't bother checking before buying because I didn't need HD, and I didn't think anyone even sold 640 x 480 video cameras any more, especially for $100 and up. However, this one is 640 x 480. Don't even bother trying the digital zoom when the resolution is that low to begin with. If mounted on a ceiling, you can flip the image so it isn't upside down, but then the pan/tilt controls are backwards. Also, the motion detection does not work at all. Tech support doesn't bother to respond, but none of these really seem fixable anyway.

Update: After a few weeks, the audio has stopped working. It is just a constant buzz. Dlink support seems nonexistent so far. Also the focus blurs itself about once a week (there is no autofocus and no way to focus remotely). You focus with a ring around the lens, and I think the panning for the camera actually works it out of focus. Not great for a remote camera.

Update2: I heard back from Dlink support. I had to go through a lot of troubleshooting with them (about an hour), but they ultimately agreed that the camera is bad and issued an RMA.

Update3: My camera has been replace. The audio is OK on the new one, and the focus ring is tighter so, once I manually focus it, it does not lose focus. I am changing the review from two to three stars based on the second camera.

title: Nice fan, very quiet!
text:
Compared to the fairly standard heatsink/fan combo that I replaced, this unit didn't cool my AMD 4400+ X2 Dual Core CPU (65 watt) by too much straight out of the box with the single fan.

When I added a second fan (SAF-B82-E1) it knocked the temp down by about 5 degrees Fahrenheit under no load & and about 10-15 degrees under 50-100% load. Another thing I noticed with a single fan is that there was a very noticeable delay of about 5 to 10 seconds in the transfer of heat from the core to the sink during CPU activity bursts so the temp spiked quite a bit before the fan caught up and started cooling the core down; with the second fan added, this delay and the spikes seem to be almost gone. I suppose the mobo's control of the fan speed could be a factor there, but it was interesting nonetheless.

The only other nit I have was the the way the clamp fit on the socket 939 bracket as it seemed to be about 1/8" to 3/16" too long, so it was a delicate balancing act to get the clamp on straight while tying it down.

One note, this did come with the snap-on mounting bracket included for the second fan (which was not included), so that was a somewhat helpful surprise.

I knocked my rating down to 4 due to the lack of a second fan & the bracket fit, otherwise it would be a 5 rating for sure. These issues aside, I would definitely recommend this as a great low cost solution to modest heat issues, just make sure you purchase the second fan!

title: Does not work on early MacOS Mojave releases
text:
Update: The last update to Mojave fixed these problems. If you still have an older version, read on (or update your OS)

I've had the BAL-M50x now for about 6 months. It's a fantastic add-on to the ATH-M50x. The sound quality is far and away the best of native bluetooth headphone I've ever tried. The battery life is a little short but I can usually get through a normal work day without issue and charge them at night. There are only two issues, one I feel is relatively minor and one which has only recently bit me and is a complete show stopper and the reason for the two star review.

Minor issue: On MacOS, when you enable the BAL-M50x for the input device, the audio output quality is reduced significantly. I've done some reading online and it seems like this is an issue with several non-Apple bluetooth headsets and is more an Apple issue than anything. I did not notice similar issues when used with my Android phone or Windows PC.

Show Stopping Issue: As of the release of MacOS Mojave (10.14) the BAL-M50x no longer works as an output device at all. It will show up in the preferences as an output and input device but no sound will come out. I've confirmed that the adapter still functions with other devices so this is strictly related to MacOS Mojave. Unfortunately, since the primary use for this adapter was for listening to music and joining video calls at work on a Macbook Pro, now running Mojave, they're completely useless for their intended purpose.

Summary: If you want the best sounding bluetooth headphones on the market, get the ATH-M50x and pair it with the BAL-M50x. Just make sure you're not on MacOS Mojave or you have updated from the release day Mojave.

title: wake-up light = good.  This light = usability disaster.
text:
The light part works, and it has helped me. It's definitely easier to wake up now, although it hasn't been the life-changing thing that other reviewers describe.

It looks nice on the nightstand, it's a nice clean design. That could be considered a plus, but it came at the cost of usability.

Everything else about this product is bad. I am confident that Philips did no user testing of this product.

1) a person or dog walking by in the bedroom can cause enough vibration to trigger the snooze function. I'm not sure if this is a manufacturing or a design defect.

2) the process for setting the clock is mediocre, reminiscent of an old 1980's digital clock. I have an iHome clock radio that's much easier to use.

3) there is no facility to set one alarm for M-F, and the other alarm for weekends. There are two alarm settings, but you must enable/disable them manually.

The worst part:

4) the controls are either touch-sensitive or they are buttons on the rim of the device. The touch sensitive ones are OK, they are slightly annoying to use but work fine. The buttons are a usability disaster. They are small, and the labels are small.

Clockwise around the rim, the buttons are: alarm 1 on/off - light dim/light on-off/light bright - radio low/ radio on-off /radio high - alarm 2 on/off. So far, not terrible, but not great. But then, there is a final button around the side that turns on some sort of test mode for the light.

So, remember #3 above. You have to set the alarm for weekends manually. I had to do this the other night. My wife was asleep so I did it in the dark. Turn off alarm 1, no problem. Reach hand around to right side to turn on alarm 2. Forget about light test button. Press light test button. Get blast of super-bright "wake up" light right in my face, right before I want to go to sleep. Also wake up wife, who is a light sleeper.

So, I would encourage Philips to redesign this light. It could be a great product. In the meantime, I encourage you to buy something else.

EDIT August 2017: I bought some [ASIN:B00EU7DBNM Sugru Moldable Glue - Black & White (Pack of 8)] and used it to help the button problems. I took a thin rolled up strip of Sugru and wrapped it around the light test button, so that you can't accidentally press the button. And I added lumps of sugru to the alarm on/off buttons so i can easily identify them in the dark. That helped a lot. The light still works as well as it ever did, so at least it's lasted this long.

May 2018: still works.

title: Won't Stream DRM-Protected Commercial Movies, But Transfers All Other Content Nearly Effortlessly
text:
In my experience, wireless storage drives are bulky, extremely difficult to set up, and not worth the effort because they won't stream purchased movies (because of DRM protection). But this SANDISK CONNECT WIRELESS STICK is totally different! It's about the size of a lipstick, is extremely easy to set up (using the Android or iOS "SanDisk Connect" app), and it (finally!) provides a simple way to transfer files (photos, music, videos, or documents) onto or off of tablets and cellphones. It still won't stream DRM-protected movies, but it does everything else you'd want a mobile wireless storage drive to do.

Once it's charged, and powered on, the SanDisk Connect Stick broadcasts a network signal. You then connect your mobile device to the Connect Stick's network, and open the SanDisk Connect app. And that's it. The app allows you to back up your Photo Gallery or Camera Roll (automatically or selectively, with or without deleting backed-up files), and allows you to transfer music, video, and document files between your mobile device and your Connect Stick (in either direction, either to or from). If you want to connect to the Internet while the Connect Stick is in use, the app has a "pass through" feature that will let you connect to the Internet via your home network, without disconnecting the Connect Stick.

The only problem I encountered was in trying to connect my PC wirelessly to the Connect Stick. You must connect the PC to the Connect Stick's network, then use a browser to go to the SanDisk Connect web site and open a display that looks like the Android or iOS app. This procedure worked for me only some of the time, and then only with the Google Chrome and MSIE browsers (never with the Firefox browser). So I would recommend setting the SanDisk Connect Stick up with a mobile app before you even attempt connecting wirelessly to a PC or Mac.

Of course, there is absolutely NO need to connect a PC or Mac to the Connect Stick wirelessly--because you can transfer your files to and from the Connect Stick directly by plugging it into a USB port on the computer. When you do that, the SanDisk Connect Stick works just like any other flash storage drive.

The SanDisk Connect Stick charges by being plugged into a computer's USB outlet, or into an AC wall adapter for USB. It cannot be charged with a USB cable. It takes about 2 hours for a full charge, and it transfers many, many files before needing to be recharged.

This is the wireless storage drive that I've been waiting for! With it, I can effortlessly transfer content (particularly photos and videos created with my tablet or cellphone cameras) directly from my mobile devices. No longer do I have to email photos or docs, simply to back them up so that they can be erased to clear space on the mobile device.

title: Works well, but not really portable
text:
I'm pretty satisfied with the performance of the Verbatim Bluetooth keyboard. Whether the keyboard is on my lap or on a hard surface, I'm able to pound away pretty quickly on it with minimal mistakes. I'm sure it helps that my hands are not unusually large (if you have a hard time typing on non-full sized keyboards, such as the ones used with netbooks, then this keyboard will probably be problematic).

There are three things that I consider design flaws with the layout of the keyboard:
1) My left pinky hits the caps lock from time to time;
2) The space bar on the right side should be wider -- the "AtlGr" key should be eliminated so it can run longer; and
3) The backspace key should be larger. I often mash a bunch of keys fumbling for it for it.

On the technical side, after the initial pairing, my iPone instantly finds the keyboard when I turn it on.

While the keyboard is pretty small when folded, it's large enough that you cannot fit in your pants pocket, and thus, has to be put it into a bag. And that's why I don't see the point of this device. One of the the central concepts behind the iPhone and iPad is that it doesn't have a physical keyboard -- everything is done through the touch screen. As soon as you need to bag to carry an accessory with you, then you might as well be carrying a laptop. I cannot imagine a situation where I would bring the keyboard with me but not my laptop -- if I'm traveling and I need to type lengthy e-mails and documents, then I'm going to bring my 13" MacBook (and it fits into a bag smaller than most handbags).

If you absolutely have to have a physical keyboard with your iPad, then you're better off getting a case for the iPad that also doubles as a keyboard, such as the [[ASIN:B004B8UZUM Gembox iPad Keyboard Case]] or [[ASIN:B004FG16MG ZAGGmate Apple iPad Accessory Case]]. At least with these you don't have a keyboard floating around that needs to be put in a bag.

title: May not have the punch of an 8", but but still best sub for the money
text:
I was a bit reluctant about buying this sub. How good can it be at the price-point? I've been using it for 30 days now and here some thoughts that might help you if you're asking yourself the same question.

Let's start with design: it's solid. The cabinet has heft to it and is not flimsy in any way. Keep in mind it's big though. If you're looking for something small and invisible this is not it. While it's not huge, it's certainly cannot be called small. I have it near a plant in a corner in my living room so I never see it, but it is big - be sure to take a look at the dimensions.

Buzz, static etc: I have not run across any humming or static when the sub is not in use. I used mediabridge's sub cables and highly recommend them. The cable is inexpensive but well made. I wonder if other reviewers who reported hum, etc, may have just been using bad cables.

Sound Quality: I'll break this down into movies and music. It performs well for both, but I do think it's more oriented towards movies and "boom" rather than fast-punch mid-bass like smaller subs. It's a 10" sub, so don't expect it to perform like an 8" when listening to music. That said though, I never feel like I made a bad choice when listening to music with it. On rare occasions I wish it was "punchier", but for 99% of the time, I think the sub just sounds great.

Bottom line: it's the best sub you'll find for the money.

Updated review:

It works just like another drive - click and drag.

Why I didn't give it five stars:
It's just about impossible to know from the file structure what order the files will play in. That's important to me because I listen to talk radio shows I download, and I want to make sure the first hour is played before the second hour, etc.

I would like to load 40 or 50 files at a time, that's the point of having 4 GB, but it's a nightmare trying to decide which ones I've listened to, and can remove, and which ones I haven't heard yet, and want to keep on.

The name that flashes across the file is not the file name in the Explorer window. And it takes a really long time for the file name to S-L-O-W-L-Y -- S-C-R-O-L-L -- A-C-R-O-S-S -- T-H-E -- S-C-R-E-E-N, so I can see the date, and maybe guess which file it is because the naming convention might have the date in the file name.

So I remove the files every 8 or 10 files, so it's a bit easier to keep track of them. I write them down, so I can then delete the correct files from Windows Explorer.

The other problem is the the fast forward/reverse button is not reliable, and sometimes, instead of fast-forwarding, it moves to the beginning of the next track, which means I have to go to the beginning of the track I was listening to, and fast forward to the point I left off, and hope the button doesn't flip out a second time, and I have to do it over again. That doesn't happen very often, but when it does, it is so frustrating!

Thanks for reminding me to update this review

title: You get what you pay for
text:
I recently purchased the Eton Elite Traveler radio for home SW tuning. It's a step up from this mini radio. I was looking for an additional radio (smaller, lighter) I could take hiking with me, so I bought the mini too. I'm happy with the mini for what it is -- an inexpensive, light, portable radio. The outdoor reception is pretty good in all bands, but beware, it does not work well indoors! Inside my home I am barely able to get 1 FM station and 1 AM station, with no SW stations. Step outside, however, and I get about 6-8 FM stations, more than a dozen or so AM stations and a decent number of SW stations. The difference is huge between indoor and outdoor reception.

I haven't had a chance to test battery life yet, but who cares... it only takes two AAA batteries and you can get rechargeables if you are really concerned about it. I like the overall interface to the radio, and the build quality is good for the price point. Speaker quality is passable. I highly recommend pairing it with a set of noise canceling headphones (Bose QC15 here) and scanning the channels outside on a chair or whatever. This is where the receiver shines, IMO -- it is in its element outdoors. Would make a great hiking, running, or camping radio.

So to sum it up for me --

Pros: Excellent size and form factor, good build quality, good reception in all bands
Cons: SW band is much more limited than I was expecting (5 – 10 MHz and 11.65 – 18 MHz), no SSB (acceptable at this price point though), no memory presets

title: JLabs J4 Buds Are Stunning
text:
I have owned a large number of ear bud style headphones over the last 25 plus years. They have been from a diverse number of manufactures including Philips, Sony, Apple, and many others. I have also had many types of full size headphones in the last 45 years including esoteric types such as electrostatic from Stax and Koss.

I have a wide range of electronic equipment from the latest, state of the art home theater to modified tube amps and electrostatic speakers. I have never heard a pair of ear buds that were in any way acceptable acoustically until I heard the JLabs J4s. The J4s are amazing, stunning buds. They come with seven sizes of ear cushions for a custom fit to your ear. The important step in obtaining the excellent sound these buds are capable of is to select the proper cushions. They must fit into your ear properly and it is worth it to take the time to find the proper fit. J4s are also the first bud with replaceable cushions that actually stay on their plastic post in all conditions. I have had many buds where the cushion has fallen off never to be seen again or have stayed in my ear when I took the buds off.

The build quality of the J4s is higher than any bud I have ever seen. The cord is truly tangle-free and the plugs and connections are reinforced for a long service life. The case that comes with them is a little on the large size but that is because it is made of very heavy duty materials. Its size does allow storage of small players with the buds.

But onto the sound. The first time I put these buds in my ear and turned on my ipod I was just blown away. I didn't think any bud was capable of sound quality like these reproduce. They actually supply bass that you can feel and the mid-range and highs are well balanced for incredible overall music balance. The sound is clear enough that you will hear stuff you have never heard before. For example, the slight delay between two drum sticks striking a drum is clearly audible - something I have never heard in other buds. Since I have had these buds I just don't want to stop listening to music. When I am listening I keep thinking that I should recommend a song that just came on as one that showcases these incredible buds. But the next song and the next song sound great as well. The overall sound is so well balanced and clear that I often can't believe that I am listening to something so small. All my sources such as several MP3 players, laptop, and other devices sound terrific with the J4s.

With the solid, strong construction, along with absolutely stunning sound I highly recommend the JLab J4 buds. They make the other buds I have like Apple, Sony, and others sound tinny and cheap. I cannot say enough good things about them.

Recently I got an idea I might be able to insert a SIM card and just log into my fantasy Football site on the go, but after owning this device for almost a year now I just found out it doesn't even have a SIM card slot. In my opinion, it is a worthless device for doing anything with Apps, or on the go. If all you need is reading books and digital newspapers, and using wifi off your home connection or Starbucks...then this might work for you. Honestly, you can get an Android device that has better App support and choices for Android, and a SIM slot for the same price or less so before you click the buy button, think about it. I love Amazon, and I love my older Kindle black and white version that looks just like real paper in a book. I actually prefer that older style paper look to read eBooks than this color screen version which hurts my eyes after a while. This was an impulse buy and I regret it. Like I said earlier, it just sits on the shelf.

title: Not at all what I was hoping for
text:
I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.

title: Great for business presentations and workshops
text:
This projector is very simple to set up and use. You'll be tempted to just plug and play, but it's important to read the manual so that you understand how placement and distance affect the quality and size of the projected image.

I don't have a lot of experience with projectors, but one thing I've come to understand is that you should choose the lumens based on your planned use of the projector. This projector is perfect for professional presentations done in a less-than-dark setting, such as a workshop or training session. Even with the lights up, you can see the projected material very clearly, and the color brightness is truly a knockout. I've had the opportunity to compare this 3000 lumen professional projector with the [[ASIN:B00EU9V3VW Epson V11H562020 PowerLite Home Cinema 2000 1080p 3LCD Projector]], and the latter is far better suited to a home cinema experience. Don't just assume that higher lumens means better. I find the [[ASIN:B00E87E1ME Epson EX6220 WXGA 3LCD Projector, 3000 lumen color, 3000 lumen white (V11H550220)]] really too bright for an evening home viewing experience, even after adjustment.

This projector comes with a professional-looking black shoulder-bag-style carrying case that makes it easy to port to sessions, and it is lightweight. You won't have to look like a dufus lugging a heavy projector around, and it has an understated look in its case that doesn't scream "steal me!" Ideally, you'd want to use a projector screen, but if you are trying to project onto a flat white or pastel (say, library or hospital or computer lab) wall, it will be fine without a screen.

Epson's projectors are consistently rated highly, whether it's the lower-end ones or those that cost thousands of dollars. You really can't go wrong with them. There is no comparison between a projector and a printer, but if this projector is as reliable as the Epson printers I have owned over the years (as I expect it to be), it will represent a very good value.

DH is the one who will be putting this projector through its paces over time, as he does workshops for writers learning to use the internet and various cloud-based software to their advantage. If he has anything negative to say about it, I will come back here and post it, but so far he's loving it. Its image is really crisp and readable, and it's truly easy to use. Bravo, Epson.

title: Great Picture, Great Value
text:
I purchased this set to replace an aging Mitsubishi 65" rear projection HDTV. I am very happy with this set. I coupled it with a Vizio 5.1 54" soundbar and the combo works well. I used the Disney WOW BluRay disc to calibrate the brightness, contrast and color and I think the set delivers a great picture. I am not a videophile, and I'm sure I could find something to nit-pick if I looked hard enough. But I think this set represents a great value.

I did run into a couple of issues: #1 is pretty trivial - with both the TV and the soundbar sitting on a piece of furniture, the soundbar blocks the IR receiver for the TV remote. I cut two 2x4 pieces of lumber and put the TV on top of those to provide some clearance. I was going to paint them to help them blend in better, but the soundbar pretty much hides them.

Issue #2 was somewhat more annoying - I could not get ARC (Audio Return Channel) to work when feeding a source through the soundbar. I originally thought it was my cable box, but I also tried with a BluRay player and could get neither to work the way I believe it is supposed to. I contacted Vizio support about 3 different times and ultimately they recommended feeding everything through the TV (all sources plug into TV). Feeding audio to the soundbar via HDMI does work as long as all sources are fed to the TV first. Vizio didn't have any explanation for this behavior.

I did run into one other issue, that is really unrelated to the TV - audio lip sync issues. Eventually I traced this to a setting in my cable box where lip sync was set to "auto" - apparently the cable box and TV are supposed to work together to set this delay. I set the lip sync setting on the cable box (Verizon FiOS VMS1000 for the record) to "off" and all is well.

Hopefully this info will help someone else.

title: The "Do Everything" Kindle Touch
text:
I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+

text:
The MHBT0545W is a simple blah, as much as you might expect, given the kind of reviews, number consumer responses, manufacture details-specs, and the retailers you would generally find these at. While trying to understand what market these are aimed towards, given the MSRP, you would think Memorex or the OEM would have given these more respect.

Packaging aside, what you find them here on Amazon, price wise is really what they are worth, or a bit less. So with that I am not that impressed. The shrink wrap is not every sophisticated and they very well might have been rewrapped. The sleeve cover slides off and reveals front flap to the headphones which sit in a velvety plastic tray. Under neath is a gold tipped red flat wire aux cable, which reminds me of the cable on the Sony MDR-V55 head phones. Also included is a micro USB charging cable. Although I had expected it, there was no carrying pouch. While doing my research I was under the impression a pouch was included. There is a 90 day warranty card, and a fold out instruction sheet, in both English and Spanish. The headphones seem to have been fully charged, as they powered up out of the box, and when I charged them they stopped charging very quickly.

They sound okay. A bit too bass for me and not clear at that. However because they have an adjustable equalizer, I prefer the treble boost setting, the most. They are not "over the ear" but more or less on the ear for me. They do well at isolating sound, the cups are soft, but the headphones keep my ears and the surrounding area warm or hot. The band has a nice plushy cushion over the head, and the cups are quite tight on my ears. I will have to see what I can do about that. The buttons are labeled well, but until I get used to them I have to take the phones off and look. So with that in mind, they are not intuitive. The lower cost model of Memorex headphones have touch controls in obvious locations on the outside ear cup - for comparisons sake, I am wondering what is up with that? These are $70 ear phones and more difficult to use.

I was able to pair them with my laptop and phone, and while connected at the same time, will switch to the source of the audio, automatically. They will not auto connect to your second device, only to the first one - which is the last device you used or paired, then you have to go to the second one and manually select connect. There is a slight gap in audio, as it detects and plays the source of sound, or start your source.

There are no voice prompts that I have noticed. The headphones have basic alert tones which do not seem very loud. Some customers will understand and appreciate what I am writing here. I will have to come back to this part and update as I get more use out of them.

Double clicking the play/pause/power button activates SIRI. However SIRI does not understand anything I say and when she speaks it's the worst quality I have ever heard. This is not particularly important, as SIRI is not an advertised feature. I will get back to this in a moment.

Conclusion, these headphones are using circuitry and a chipset, meant for $80+ headphones. Although not mentioned, they are using a CSR 8645 chipset which by specification, can multi-point connect to two phones or other combination of bluetooth audio sources. They do not advertise what codecs are supported but again by definition the chipset is meant to support Apt-X, Low Latency, and ACC, please see [...] for reference. I am led to believe, they use the chip for it's most basic features, Bluetooth 4.1, half of the available slots meant for equalizer settings, and nothing else. SIRI sounding as bad as she does, is a victim of this basic configuration, and I am surprised she actually does anything at all.

The phones look good, sound okay and worth the amount of money I paid for them. However I will be buying something else at some future date, as the bluetooth headphone market matures.

Number two, I installed the driver on my laptop running Windows 10 and other than a blip during the installation process (screen went blank/black, and the computer froze - had to do a hard reboot) the driver and the tablet seems to be working fine. However - I also want to use this tablet on my desktop computer which is running Windows 7 Pro (yeah I know it's old). So I downloaded the driver off the website as before and installed the driver - it sort of worked, but I got a Windows message that says it's an "unsigned" driver and should be uninstalled. So for right now I'm just going to use the tablet with my laptop.

The tablet works great - I haven't dug into the manual much yet as to reassigning the programmable controls but I plan on doing that soon. I've got a number of drawing/graphics software on both my machines and have only tested the tablet out with what I have on my laptop. The tablet works a bit differently depending on what program you're using. Surprisingly the program that I found that works best is the inexpensive open source Krita software that I got for like $10 from the Epic Games store. Painter Essential 7 also worked pretty good - but I kept having problems (which might be due to not configuring the pen and controls settings).

I need to spend more time messing with the tablet and the different software to see what it really can do. Right now - I'm very happy with my purchase.

title: Amazon Basics Versus Kantek -- Who Offers The Best Platform For The Price?
text:
I would have thought that this was a great unit if I hadn't just bought a Kantek platform a week earlier. It's still a good unit for the average user but the Kantek gets my vote -- and here's why: Both units are made of a durable black plastic. The Kantek unit is longer and wider and its height is more adjustable because of the different sized blocks provided for the legs. In addition the Kantek can be raised to a platform height of 6.5 inches while the Amazon Basics unit maxes out at 4.875 inches. The increased length., width, and height of the Kantek platform provides slightly more storage under the platform and gives the user more flexibility in what to put there.

The Kantek unit also has inserts in the back of the platform to allow the cords/cables used to hook up a monitor or TV to be neatly organized. On the positive side, the Amazon Basics unit is sturdier because of how the legs are constructed -- in long single units rather than individual blocks like the Kantek. The last item is the price difference. The Amazon Basics unit wins the price war at $19.99 versus the Kantek being offered at $22.99. To me the small price advantage of the Amazon Basics platform is negated by the wider footprint, more flexible (and maximum) height adjustment, and cable management offered by the Kantek platform. It all depends on what your individual needs are. You really can't go wrong with either choice.

title: Great basic computer
text:
This is a fairly basic desktop computer by today's standards. It's powerful enough for most of your everyday computing needs, as well as for occasional graphic design and photo editing. It can also handle basic video editing. It does struggle if you're doing complex video editing with large files. It's also not recommended for video games that require a much more powerful unit.

Fortunately, there is room to upgrade or add components to this unit to make it more powerful. You can double the memory to 16GB. You can add a solid state drive for faster storage access (highly recommended to improve the overall performance). You can add a dedicated graphics card if you want to improve video editing and play power-hungry video games. You'll probably need to upgrade the power supply as well to handle more cards and drives. You'll need to break the warranty seal to gain access to the chassis to do any upgrades. And you'll definitely want to add a chassis fan since none is included (ASUS should have really included one). If you're going to do all these upgrades, you should probably just buy a more powerful unit to begin with, or build your own computer from scratch. For the same price, you can build a more powerful computer with better components, if you have the knowledge.

As a basic computer, it performs great. It's solid and speedy when multitasking with web browsers, office programs, Spotify, etc. Streaming from Netflix is no problem. WiFi is fast and solid. And it's fairly quiet since there is no chassis fan.

title: Fantastic Binoculars For The Price
text: A family friend - himself a relatively accomplished skipper - had brilliant Steiner 7x50mm binoculars, which I always adored, but could never afford.  I've been fortunate enough to come into possessing these Tasco OffShore 36 binoculars, as a gift for a job well done, and I feel that envy subside.  For weeks, now, they've served me well.  The compass is as accurate as any in my collection, and calculating distance is now a breeze with or without the use of the built-in slip-ring scale.  Optics are bright and clear, in all weather, faring well in my own informal PVT test (rough distance with a modest photocopy of the chart).  The compass and reticle are easy to read.  The objective lens caps are connected to the center pivot, making them hard to lose.  About the only thing I wasn't wild about, was the big rubber rear boot that rarely stays in place.  I aim to replace it with individual caps, when the opportunity presents itself.  But that's hardly a deal breaker.  In all, it's the best set of optics I've owned, and I would recommend it to most people.  In my experiences, my Tasco OffShore 36 binoculars compare favorably to binoculars costing twice as much.  Even if they weren't a gift, I would pay the asking price, knowing I'm getting a great deal.

text:
I ordered 'Lenovo IdeaPad 3 14" Laptop, 14.0" FHD 1920 x 1080 Display, AMD Ryzen 5 3500U Processor, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 256GB SSD, AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics, Narrow Bezel, Windows 10, 81W0003QUS, Abyss Blue' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

First off if you are looking for a gaming beast of a laptop, this is not it. However if you are looking for a laptop that will mainly be used for web browsing, Netflix streaming, office document creating and some light gaming, this laptop does great. The only game that I have tried with this, (besides Solitaire) is Diablo lll and it did just fine. With that said, I would not recommend using this for gaming as it just does not have the hardware to support it. There seems to only be one RAM slot and no other hard drive slots to upgrade for more internal storage as you can see in the attached images.

Now with that out of the way, I will list some of the features I really like.
It's light weight and small enough to fit in most backpacks.
It has a built in privacy slider for the built in camera.
It is a solid build quality.
It runs Windows 10 very well and has been stable with every windows update so far.
It has an HDMI port.
It has a good amount of USB A ports (3).
It has a built in SD card reader slot.

Overall this has been a great little laptop for my use and I think it has good value if you understand the limitations. One thing that I do wish it had was a USB C port. Other than that it has been solid and reliable laptop that I mainly use for browsing the web, video chat, streaming movies and very light gaming.

text:

This caused a lot of problems and I was constantly transferring my images to an external HDD and it was extremely inconvenient.

I decided to purchase this USB flash drive. It was low cost for such a large amount of space. Best decision I ever made!
I have had this in my laptop for the last 2 months and it has not fallen out or gotten damaged. I carry my laptop everywhere with me.
Data transfers are very fast. With less than 50 picutures, it's basically instant and I often feel the need to check and make sure the files actually transferred because it happens so quickly, I don't even get a "Transferring files" window. I have never had a failed transfer.

If you are using it in a mac, you will need to reformat it to ExFAT. It will work out of the box, but will not accept large folders or files until it is reformatted.

The only issue I've ever had is if my computer falls asleep, the drive will sometimes disconnect, but that is due to the settings on my computer and not the drive. A simple unplug-replug reconnects it.

The one design element I do not like is that the tiny red light to indicate it is powered on is not visible unless one is looking down from almost directly overhead. I much prefer a power strip that has the indicator light incorporated in the switch, or at least has an indicator light that protrudes so it may be seen from across the room.

title: Fake dummy cam that we hope may deter people
text: 102. My first thoughts when I seen the CCTV Dummy Camera was that it actually looked pretty realistic. It isn't too far off from my own security companies cameras that circle my home. The exterior of the camera is black in color. I watched the video tips on how to get your dummy camera ready to use before installing it outside of my home. You will need to have the internet to watch it. The instruction videos I watched were very easy to follow. I installed the batteries and mounted the dummy camera without any problems. All the mounting hardware is included with the camera. You do require a screwdriver to set up to install the dummy camera. First prior to installing I put the 2 AAA batteries into the camera. The batteries are to make the red LED light flash in 5 second intervals. This is what makes the dummy camera appear to be realistic to a passerby. Sure people can bypass advanced systems but the dummy hopefully will make them think twice. This camera is meant as a deterrent only. There are no wires to deal with for the most part, other than a real short piece of one. You tuck it into the soffit. Soffit is on your roof and is typically 12 inches wide and made from center lanced U groove perforated sections of vinyl in a return fashion and fixed to a truss roofing system. Just mount the camera either to the wall or onto the soffit and screw into the roof trusses. Most roof truss systems have enough overhang allowance for this. The camera can be used indoor or outdoors and is apparently waterproof. I had friends come over to visit my grandmother. That is who the dummy camera is babysitting. I thought it would be amusing to prank them into thinking she has a camera for real. They were amazed when I told them that the camera was a dummy camera. The blinking red LED light is what really makes people believe it is real. That is what a few close friends commented when they seen it at my grandma's house. If you cannot afford to buy a real home security system the dummy camera is a good second choice. The camera has a roof over the mechanism parts to keep the rain and weather out of the camera. The camera is very lightweight and looks even more realistic at nighttime. The camera could also be used with a real home security system in places where you don't have a camera but want it to appear like a camera is there. There was no screwdriver included with this one in the box. I received this product free in return for a review and my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: Try this 16 GB recorder first!  BEST RECORDER with professional sound quality at AMAZING PRICE!
text:
I tested this device while…
At Startbucks having a conversation about parenting with by husband during their weekday morning rush. Recorder was sitting on the table 3 ft away from each of our mouths.
Using the voice activated recorder while in the bath/shower when I came up with something I needed to write down but couldn’t.
A lecture meeting with a lot of other laptops running
My office with all hardwood floors and no rugs yet

Very Durable:
When I first received the box, I noticed how small it was so I figured this recorder would be light weight and I wasn’t sure what to expect. I was very shocked after I pulled the recorder our and held it. It is a lot heavier than I was expecting (in a good way) and it’s actually very durable and hasn’t broken when I have dropped it twice now. I dropped it once in a parking lot then I accidentally kicked it while walking and the other was onto my bathroom floor. It still works great!

Auto Save Function:
Because let’s face it, we need this!
It’s rechargeable via USB and USB connects to Mac or Windows making it super easy to transfer and save or transfer to transcribe.

Voice Activated Recorder:
Voice activated means no more snippets of silence or distracting sounds ruining your recording. This feature is AMAZING! You can switch this mode on or off at any time. The recorder will automatically start recording when sound is detected. If there is no sound or a humming noise like a bathroom fan or some chatter in the background like at Starbucks, the device will pause recording. It will be flashing when recording so you know when it is recording and when it is paused. This function was so neat to play with to see what kicked it on and off. This function is AWESOME if you want to save memory space and also not to have to sit through long pauses of thinking or a lecture or whatever. .

Noise Reduction Mode:
This is my 2nd favorite feature because you can also turn this feature on or off. While I was sitting at a Starbucks and having a conversation with my husband, I actually wanted the sounds of the coffee being made in the background since this was a conversation that I’m going to be turning into a podcast. This was awesome because you could hear us loud and clear but it didn’t sound like we were in a recording booth, it sounded like real life but not in a distracting way. LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS FUNCTION!!!

Screen:
This LED screen is extremely easy to read and operate even if you are like me and want to try and figure gadgets out on your own first without reading the instructional manual. The menu system itself is the easiest to navigateI I also love how I can see the sound wavelengths when I’m listening back to content so I know when something is about to be said and also if I’m close to peaking. I can also see the wavelengths on the screen while I’m recording so I know if I’m too close to the microphone or if I’m talking too loud. I can also judge how distracting the background noise is while recording also! This is very important to me because in the past with other recorders, I thought the background noise wasn’t that loud and I go home and listen to what I had done that day and there is no much background noise that it is extremely difficult to focus on what I’m saying, This was incredible annoying. I also missed some lecture notes because someone’s laptop fan was running and the professor sounded drowned out. If this has happened to you, I’m sorry and I understand, and get this recorder so it won’t happen again!

Battery Life:
I only charged it once and that was when it first came in and I've recorded up to 5 hours total!!!

I will be updating this review with a link to the podcast that my husband and I recorded while in Starbucks so you can see how amazing this little but mighty recorder actually is!

title: Comfortable and fast.
text:
It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.

title: it easily deserves 5 stars
text: For what it is, a 20 watt practice amp, it easily deserves 5 stars. The quality of the build and the number of features you get are awesome at this price point. With the on board models, EQ, ability to switch between class A/AB, ability to adjust the bass bias, and both a master volume and power knob, along with the preamp gain control you have great ability to fine tune the amp and get the sound you want out of it and it's very versatile. Even better, it sounds great at low volumes that don't tick off my wife or neighbors and it can be used with your standard head phones (no quarter inch required). The built in noise gate is nice feature as I love my single coil guitars, and the built in tuner keeps your practice session moving. The onboard effects aren't necessarily going to compete with any of your dedicated pedals but they're significantly better than those included on most amps and fun to mess around with while you're practicing. You're not going to faithfully reproduce the sound of Brain May's AC30 or get the same punch and breakup as you would out of a cranked JCM800, but what reasonable person would expect to from a 20 watt combo? If you're looking for a well made, versatile, practice/home recording amp at a reasonable price point you can't go wrong here.

title: Solid Sound Profile
text:
The current trend with ear buds is to boost the bass to the point of overpowering the rest of the sound profile. I don’t particularly like bass that is too heavy because it can give me awful headaches. These buds have the bass boosted but it is not over the top.

These ear buds are very lightweight and low profile. Smaller than many ear buds I have used they fit in my ears very comfortably. The silicone inserts are soft and do not cause any discomfort, but just as important they create a good seal in the ear canal and as a result they have good passive noise canceling (sound isolation). This is a good sign right out of the package - many ear buds I have tried do not seal properly.

The sound profile is the most important aspect of any earphones or ear buds. There are really three areas in the sound profile that merit mention - the highs, the mids and the bass. This set of buds is marketed as heavy bass and that is not completely true. Yes, they do have good bass, but it is not heavily overdriven like most. The bass is a little more front-and-center, not in-your-face, if that makes some sense. The mids are good and the music sounds full as a result, not hollow and depthless. The highs are very bright and clear which is a slight surprise - most ear buds that enhance the bass do so at the expense of the highs, so having a set that had strong bass and highs together is a very nice change of pace.

These buds come with a very small carrying case. It is a pinch case and has enough room for just the buds and the replacement silicone inserts. It is a soft plastic case and provides protection only from dirt and moisture (though by no means waterproof) so this is not a case that will help when the buds are crammed in a pocket or backpack.

This is a very nice set of ear buds at a very nice asking price. They have a very good sound profile and they are comfortable to wear. Keep these in mind when looking for inexpensive buds and good sound.

I believe it is sending a 1080 sized feed to the computer, but the actual camera itself looks less sharp than 720 scaled up to 1080. I'd say it is better than those uber-cheap 480p cameras, but it is definitely NOT the resolution they claim. Secondly, this is a wide angle lens with a lot of distortion as you reach the borders of your frame. See included photo for examples of the fish-eye edge distortion. The microphone isn't all that great either, but that's to be expected when the mic is so far away from you. For good audio, I always recommend a desk mic instead of a webcam mic anyway. All in all, if you just need to show up for work meetings or classrooms on zoom, this will do the job just fine! But if you want to look professional, record a vlog or twitch stream, etc, you're going to want a webcam with better quality, resolution, and less lens distortion.

text:
Just needed a throwaway pair of headphones, was pleasantly surprised.
