title: Nice Smaller Bendy-Leg Tripod
text:
This is marketed as a tripod designed for the Nest camera, but I didn’t get it for that particular use. Instead, I selected it for two purposes – first as a low-profile support for a video light and second as a tabletop tripod mount for my camera that will fit in my camera bag. It is a decent little tripod, not perfect but good for my purposes.

This is a small-profile tripod, measuring about 12” (a little more) when folded up as it comes from the package. It is fully assembled and is completely ready to go. The legs are initially straight; they are bendy though and can be adjusted some to increase/decrease the height as well as wrap around things to secure the tripod in place.

The head has a standard mounting screw so it will fit most cameras and similar accessories. My video light uses this size of screw so it attaches very easily and securely to the tripod. There is an adjustment ring on the mounting screw that allows for getting the mount tight against the device to which it is attached, even when the whole screw does not fit. The head also has a ball joint so that it can tilt the device in any direction and secure it without issue.

It works a bit better than other bendy-leg tripods I have used. It seems to be more stable in most situations. In particular, when the legs are wrapped around something and it is suspended off the ground, it doesn’t slip quite as readily, though with enough weight it can be shifted which should be fairly obvious.

The one area where this tripod could be improved is in the feet at the ends of the legs. These are smooth, rubber feet and most of the time they’re adequate for keeping the tripod stable and still. That said, on an modest incline they are not non-slip enough to keep the tripod from shifting, especially when on a moving surface (I know, this is an unusual circumstance, but it does happen occasionally). It’s easy enough to work around this with some tacky adhesive like you might find in a classroom, but it would be nice if this wasn’t necessary. On smoother inclined surfaces there are better solutions.

This is a nice little tripod that works reasonably well. It is not perfect but it does work better than a lot of other small, bendy-leg tripods. It’s made well and it fits nicely in my camera bag. Consider this one if you are looking for a small tripod.

title: Best one
text:
Before getting this keyboard, I tried the Logitech solar keyboard and the Moko for the iPad mini. They both had their drawbacks.

The Moko keyboard/cover is very small, with the keys very close together. I could have gotten used to that, but the space bar is defective. It's only about two inches wide, but if you don't press it right in the middle, it will not create a space. It's tricky - almost impossible - to put your thumb in the right place so that you hit the space bar right on the center, every single time. The other problem is the = key is right where the delete key usually is (if you are a touch typist). So instead of deleting, you get a lot of unwanted ====es. I finally had to give up. I also am using a Moko wraparound suede case, which is actually perfect, and this keyboard/cover combination conflicts with that. You can't use the keyboard as it is intended if you keep the Moko cover on the iPad Mini.

The Logitech solar keyboard is a great idea - no batteries, ever - but it is quite large (mostly to accommodate the solar panel). It's only about 1/2 inch wider than the wireless Apple keyboard, which I could live with, but it's 2 inches higher at the top. It's also pretty hefty. The size and weight are just not practical for traveling.

I'll find other uses for these keyboards.

The Amazon keyboard, on the other hand, is perfect. It's light, the keys are just where you expect them to be, it's about a half inch less wide and less tall than the Apple wireless keyboard. It pairs easily. The keys feel very similar to the Apple keyboard. We'll see how long the AAA batteries last, but I'm not worried; it's easy to carry a few spares. The "connect" and "on/off" buttons are on the bottom and are very clearly marked.

The travel stand turned out to be a pleasant surprise. The iPad Mini fits perfectly into the stand, even with the Moko case on it (although only with the cover of the case set off from the Mini - it won't fit into the grove if the front flap of the cover is right up against the Mini). Because I don't have to take the cover off the Mini, when I pick up the Mini I can read it like a book, as always, with the built-in hand strap, which is what the Moko cover is designed to let you do. The tips of the legs of the stand are coated with rubber, so it stays nicely in place. It doesn't feel or look like cheap plastic, which was what I was expecting.

Overall, this keyboard and its little stand convinced me that, once again, Amazon paid attention to the details and came up with a high-quality product that does exactly what it is supposed to do, and elegantly.

But I've also tried these with my android tablet and Kindle - the headphones work but the controller doesn't (which is to be expected).

My one and only complaint about these, is that you just get a soft cloth bag to store these in. Since I'm carrying these around in my backpack, I wanted something a bit more protective. So I searched here on Amazon for a case and didn't find anything that looked suitable. Then I walked around the local big-box store to see if I could find something that could be repurposed. I looked through all the departments. I had high hopes of finding a camera case, but none were the right size and proportions. I finally found something that was perfect. Cutting through the health and beauty department, I spotted a clear plastic shaving bag that was meant for travelers. It was heavy duty plastic and the exact size needed to store these headphones. title: Delightful.
text:
Update: I do really like this computer. It has smoothly integrated into my home network and I now quickly go to it for quick and easy browsing and/or controlling stuff in my house (particularly if the main computer is in use by somebody else or for some reason tethered. The great thing is that with the full power of Windows and third party software, it can be whatever you need it to be. The one negative I've found, though, is that the delete key is under the backspace key where you expect backslash to be (which is in turn beside the right alt key). For this reason, I've accidentally went into sleep mode a few times, which is annoying. You can turn off the power key (while running) in windows, but the delete key still isn't where it is supposed to be.

Original review:

Surprise! I actually love this computer.

I mean, I am a bit of a power user, so I have a big gaming laptop and a couple of servers throughout my house, not to mention a few purpose-built niche laptops. So while I was a bit skeptical of this machine before it came since I saw the low price tag, I think it's awesome for the right purpose.

I mean, I totally get what "Chrome Books" are trying to do - be low price, low weight computers that run basically "from the cloud". But who really wants a computer running Android? I mean, there are phones for that. So running Windows 10 is a great idea. (Not that I love Windows 10, but if you install Windows Classic Shell and tweak, tweak, tweak away...turn off all permissions, get rid of all the stupid crap they're trying to sell you, use an offline account, then it is almost as good as Windows 7).

Anyway, you don't get a lot of fancy new stuff, but what you do get is important: 1080p screen, mini-HDMI out (odd choice, would have gone for micro or even full, but whatever), 2 USB 3.0 (No C), a micro-SD card reader, headphone jack, and a M.2 expansion port.

64GB of ROM is pretty small, but they installed so little bloatware (just one program to make the touchpad better - I uninstalled it because I didn't recognize it, am paranoid, and figure I can adjust it with whatever is built into Windows) that you have ~45GB free. Should be enough for stuff like MS office and other junk you may want. But you know what, I have a 36TB NAS, and Windows works flawlessly with it, so if I'm using this as a home machine, it's not a problem. I don't much care for public cloud, so if I want to take this on the road, I can always stream (usually still reach my NAS) or just throw in an SSD (by the way, it only takes the small form factor) or a giant micro-SD card (although admittedly either of these factors takes away the fact that this item is inexpensive to begin with.

6GB of RAM is sufficient for a computer that is not meant to be a workhorse.

It's really thin and light and with a real keyboard is just delightful as opposed to dealing with a tablet; a tablet always disappoints me when I'm trying to get something done quickly. It also boots up fast due to NAND memory. It doesn't even look cheap or anything. It actually looks pretty good.

It has a regular "wall wart" type AC adapter instead of the usual laptop power brick. I like this, but the cord is a little short (on the other hand, it is likely easily replaced with something in my electronics closet) The barrel adapter goes into the right side of the device (which is not abnormal, but less normal than the back or the other side in my experience) and the unfortunate part is that it will partially fit into the stereo mini-plug port for headphones on the same spot on the other side, which is likely to cause some confusion.

The only apparent downside is that the keyboard seems...like it vibrates slightly. Like it's not held in tight enough or something. I mean, it does have nice keys and overall I like it, but it just feels slightly weird, although still much better than a tablet roll-out keyboard.

I actually really like this little machine. Not for my main computer or my only computer, but definitely for easy browsing, or a multimedia machine for a teen, or a school computer, a travel computer, whatever. I'd use it for plenty of things, happily.

If you're cool with the memory - and living off a NAS, an SD card, or the cloud - and you're looking for something small and usable, definitely give this some consideration.

title: Sony - C400 Wireless Behind-Neck In Ear Bluetooth Headphones.
text:
I guess the type of Bluetooth headphones a person buys depends on how they want to use them. For a super-full, high quality sound I would think over the ear headphones would be the best. But for talking on the phone and doing what I like to do - lie on the couch watching YouTube videos- these behind the neck are absolutely the best. I had been wearing over the ear headphones for months and after a few hours the outside of my ears would ache from the pressure of even the soft cups of the headphones (which are very high quality and expensive). And I would struggle trying to get in a comfortable position while wearing them.

These behind the neck in-ear headphones take some getting used too but are so much easier to wear. Once I finally got used to the idea that all the controls are beside my neck and not on my ear cup, lying on the couch surfing the internet and watching YouTube became a much better experience. They connected almost instantly to my laptop, and once I became familiar with how all the buttons worked it was easy to use them. I have fallen asleep several times and never woke up with sore ears. The sound is almost as good as the over the ears headphones, but I like these more for podcasts and talk radio shows.

The battery life is outstanding. I have had these turned on for several hours at a time for three nights in a row and the battery check voice level still tells me that the battery level is high. There is really nothing negative I can find to say about these behind the neck in ear headphones. They are very lightweight, comfortable, have good sound, connected quickly to all my devices, come with different sized ear bud covers, and are a cool blue. If I should have any problems with them later I will update this review but for now I think they are fantastic.

UPDATE 10.8.17 - I've used these headphones for nearly every night since I got them and they have never once, disconnected from my streaming source. My older headphones dropped me off a lot so it's really super nice to never have to re-connect. Also, they seem to have a greater distance of reception than my other headset. It can be setup wired or wireless (built in battery). Not entirely sure how long the battery lasts as I mind weird. Just messing around with it before mounting it the battery lasted for sometime. The battery mounted option would be great for someone that is renting and doesn't want to premaritally mount the door bell.

Setup was fairly painless. Using the included mount bracket and screws it went pretty quickly. Note for the wise. If you have a stucco house do not over tighten the screws on the mounting plate. This can cause the mounting plate to bend. Then the door bell itself will not align and mount up correctly. Make sure the bracket is level and strait. With the app downloaded it was just a matter of pressing the orange button on the back and away it went. Created and account and joined it to my WiFi and never looked back! The easiness of the setup means the none tech minded could easily set this up.

The doorbell works reliably. When pressed the push notifications are quick and timely. There is a little lag when first connecting to the session. Once connected its responsive an quick. You can clearly hear the person and see them. Likewise on their end the speaker is loud and they can hear you clearly. This is especially great for the solicitors that cannot seem to be bothered by your no soliciting sign. This also has the ability to act as a motion detection camera of sorts. If motion is detected it will send you a push notification and you can watch whats happening with out answering the motion. If there is indeed someone there that didn't press the doorbell but knocked on your door instead you can answer it just like the regular doorbell and talk with them. The motion alerts take some tweaking and are not exactly perfect but come in very handy.

Ring customer service is fantastic! I would recommend this product just for the fantastic customer service ring has. Living in the desert the doorbell see's a fair amount of sun in the afternoons. As a result the center press portion of the doorbell fell off. Ring sent out a replacement quickly. I was sincerely impressed with their service on this issue. That alone makes me feel confidant in this product.

I would recommend this product to friends and family.

title: Consolidation is a beautiful thing
text:
The perfect external 3.5" hard drive for purchase at this point in time as far as I'm concerned: they include controller software *if you want it*, but they don't try to persuade you to use it, instead taking the simplistic approach, which is plug it in and use it! I would never use software to run a hard drive anyway.

Also, 4TB seems to be the sweet spot right now for price/size ratio for external 3.5" storage (3.5" drives always require an external power source, whereas 2.5" external drives - which are sometimes slower - usually do not). I like that you can leave it plugged in, but it only powers on when you attach the USB cable.

USB 3.0 really is a vast improvement over previous versions. I'm dumping all my files from five other drives on this monster, and 500GB are transferring through the computer from one drive to another in around 2-3 hours, both large and tiny files.

Worth noting is that the case seems very thin around the drive, which is probably good for heat dispersion, but will not provide the kind of protection you'd want if you were constantly transporting this drive.

I now have on here hundreds of seasons of TV shows, most in HD, nearly a thousand movies, most in HD, hundreds of music albums, books, maps, comics, software setup files, etc., and I STILL have room to grow. To get all these things consolidated and organized - and all accessible with a single drive powered up - is really fantastic.

title: It lives up to the hype.
text:
This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.

title: Was so pleasantly surprised by these
text: I have tried just about any and all earbuds/headphones for listening to music and audio books and most of them have pros and cons.  Over the ear have amazing sound, but those big "cups" cause the ear area to sweat so must be removed from time to time to "air out."  Earbuds...I love earbuds and have a couple of pairs that have astounding sound, but unfortunately, I have some odd ear canals - maybe to shallow, not curved enough or something as I can only wear them a short time before they end up falling out.  On-ear tend to be my favorite - they don't press down on the ear, they hook over the top so they stay in place and are comfortable to wear for a long period of time.  Their main problem (as is the same with all those mentioned above) is that they block the ear canal from hearing sounds around the individual that can be important.  Enter bone conduction headphones - they transmit sound through the bone just in front of the ear canal yet keep the ear canal open to sounds around the individual which is great for runners, warehouse workers, and others that do need to be aware of cars/machinery and others around them.  I mention all of this to explain I have had just about every type of earbud/headphone out there and these instantly became my hands down favorites the moment I put the synced pair on and played music and a portion of an audio book.  They are SO COMFY to wear!  These are sort of a cross between earbuds and bone conduction - the hooks that go over the ear place the piece over the ear canal, but it does not wholly cover it, so you can still hear what's going on around you.  I didn't mention that I also have neck speakers which are great if you are sitting, working on your computer - the neck speakers do mean that unless you keep the speaker volume low, everyone around you gets to hear whatever you are listening to.  That's fine - sometimes - but that's why these open ear headphones are perfect - private music/book reading and yet if someone steps into your cubicle, you can still hear them talking to you.  These have nudged my on-the-ear headphones out as my favorites.  I think the only thing I might suggest as a change to the manufacturer is a notch in the formed case that would make it easier to pick them up.  The formed section for each ear piece is very snug and I have had a little trouble getting them out with stubby fingers (and fingernails) - I used the edge of safety-tipped scissors to nudge them out of their "bed" in the case.  That's really just a little thing considering.

title: Difficult to Install, But Provides Good Drop Protection
text:
Because this BLOK PROTECTIVE SHELL FOR IPAD AIR2 is a Logitech product, I trust the manufacturer's claim that it protects an iPad Air2 from 6-foot drops. I'm certainly not going to test the claim by intentionally dropping my tablet! I ordered this protective shell after my husband dragged my iPad Air2 off the dining room table onto a chair, and the tablet nearly landed on the ceramic tile floor that breaks everything that falls onto it.

Inserting the iPad Air2 into the BLOK shell was very difficult--it took about 20 minutes. You must follow the instructions and start with the tablet's top corners inserted into the shell, because the hard rubber must be worked around the tablet edges inch by inch. I used a metal spudger tool (on hand for opening mobile device cases) to help, but of course I risked scratching the iPad Air2 case. (I don't think I did.) Clearly it will be equally difficult to remove the hard rubber shell, so you don't want to try this product unless you're really in need of drop protection.

The shell comes with a screen protector, which I didn't need because my iPad Air2 already had one. The shell adds weight to the tablet--definitely more weight than my "official" [[ASIN:B00OO9X4O2 Apple iPad Air 2 Smart Case]]--but I'm willing to accept that to get the drop protection. My tablet lives on a tabletop, but if I should need to travel with it, I will carry it in a protective sleeve (like the [[ASIN:B004Y20KU0 rooCASE Apple iPad Air Sleeve Case Cover]]) that covers the glass. The BLOK provides shock absorption, but has no screen cover.

title: W-King X10 Versus Others, And The Winner Is....
text:
Updated 12/19/21:
SOUNDCORE MOTION BOOM VERSUS W-KING X10
I gave into temptation and bought the much revered Motion Boom by Anker/Soundcore to compare it against the X10. If you go on YouTube you'll see a ton of videos on both speakers. I was curious to see if the Motion Boom is the real deal. To keep the comparison fair, I used my custom equalizer settings in the VLC app to play music downloaded and stored on my phone. So...the same equalizer was used to test both Bluetooth speakers. (BTW, there's a lot of fanfare given to Soundcore's equalizer that is in their app. But after spending hours upon hours trying out Soundcore's EQ versus VLC's, I got the best deep bass AND clarity with VLC). I probably spent 10 hours over the span of 2 weeks comparing both speakers. The verdict: By a small margin, the X10 sounds better. The biggest difference is that the bass from the X10 is a bit fuller and richer. Not much, but noticeable nonetheless. And the X10 gets a little bit louder as well. Overall, the X10 is a really good speaker. Built like a tank. But, the Motion Boom is incredibly impressive for it's size (smaller than the X10). I ended up keeping the Motion Boom. Got it at a good price during Cyber Monday. So I'm having fun alternating my use of the X10 and Motion Boom. :)

Updated 8/28/21:
As mentioned below in my original review, I ordered the T9-1 and have done a pretty thorough comparison of features and sound quality between the X10 and T9-1. Heaviest emphasis is on sound quality. The verdict: The X10 wins. Yes, the T9-1 has an ever-so-slightly deeper bass than the X10. But for you bass lovers, the difference is barely discernible. And the T9-1 bass has a weird, kind of unpleasant hollow sound to it that I do not notice with the X10. The bass on the T9-1 just doesn't sound as crisp and clear as the X10. Maybe the larger casing with the T9-1 causes that hollow sound? Not sure. Anyway, the T9-1 does get a little bit...again, only a little bit...louder than the X10. Again, barely discernible. Overall, I just think the X10 sounds better and combine that with the fact that the X10 is IPX6 rated, the X10 is an overall better speaker. (I do like the lighting effects on the T9-1 and that it auto-shuts off after a while if there's no music input. But for me, sound quality is most important.)

Original review:
I've become a bluetooth speaker junky. I've owned about a dozen of them over the years and currently have 4, with a 5th one (a W-King T9) on the way.
I purchased this W-King X10 a couple of weeks ago and it sounds great. I also have several Doss speakers including 2 Doss Soundbox XL's that are probably the best bang for the buck as far as getting really good sounding speakers at a low price. Paired together, the 2 Doss XL's sound fantastic with their sub-woofers providing low bass, but (a) they are for indoor use only and (b) the W-King X10 is louder with even deeper bass.

So, now that I've had the W-King X10 for a couple of weeks, here are the pros and cons:

PROS
> Excellent sound. I'm a bass lover and this speaker does not disappoint.
> Solidly built. This speaker is put together like a tank. Good looking too.
> Very resistant to water damage, but not submersible.
> Good value for the price.

CONS
> I wish bluetooth speaker manufacturers/resellers wouldn't exaggerate the battery duration in their product descriptions. For example, W-King says the X10 can last 45 hours on one charge. Well that may be true, but read the caveat carefully in the description. It says 45 hours if it's on the lowest volume setting. Heck...you can hardly hear anything on the lowest volume setting. So no way does this battery last as long as it's hyped if you intend to use it as most people would, i.e. at 50% - 75% volume. At those higher volume settings, I'd say you'll get between 5-8 hours of playtime.
> I like using the TF/SD card feature. But I wish the unit would automatically shuffle the files instead of playing them in sequence. I contacted the reseller and they said there's no firmware update available to shuffle the TF/SD card playlist. (The Doss XL does have a firmware update that shuffles music files being played from a TF/SD card.)
> There's no auto-off feature that turns off the speaker if there's no incoming bluetooth signal after...say...10 minutes.

Lastly, to those who have given lower ratings because the X10 does not come with a power adapter/charger, you're certainly entitled to do so. But the description clearly states, multiple times, that this speaker does not come with an adapter/charger. So it's not like they didn't tell you! And besides, probably 90% of us already have adapters/chargers that we can use for the X10. It can handle up to a 30 watt adapter/charger for the quickest charging time (3.5 hrs). I don't have one, so I just use an existing 10 watt adapter/charger. Yeah...it takes longer to charge, but I just plug it in at bedtime and it's fully charged by morning.

So, I can't wait for the T9 to arrive and then I'll compare the two and update this review. Stay tuned!!

title: Easy setup, fast speeds, great price. What more could you want?
text:
I received this as a gift for my birthday after adding it my wishlist. So far, I am extremely impressed. I'm replacing an old Medialink 802.11n router (the company apparently went under years ago). The Medialink router worked fine, I didn't have any disconnecting issues, but the range was somewhat poor and I wanted more speed. Boy, did this do the trick. I play a lot of games on Steam, and use Steam download speeds as a way to measure my connection in some cases. On my old Medialink router, I downloaded games between 2 and 4 MB/S. After getting the TP-Link router up and running, I'm downloading games between 18 and 22 MB/S. A massive improvement. I also purchased a TP-Link AC1900 USB 3.0 adapter which also made a big difference. Basically, I had a huge bottleneck in my system on my old 802.11n router with a USB 2.0 adapter. I had been paying for internet speed that I wasn't even capable of using with my old hardware.

The setup was dead simple and I had no issues. I was connected to the internet within about 2 minutes of plugging the unit in. The web-based interface was easy to understand and seemed to have a lot of configuration options. I was able to get some of my IP-based home security cameras up and running on the new network in a matter of minutes with the simple to use port forwarding menus. I'm not an advanced network user by any means, but everything has been buttery smooth so far (and I'm on Windows 10).

As far as range goes, I used to get a somewhat weak signal on my old router in an upstairs bedroom. Now I get 100% connectivity at all times anywhere in my home (which granted is somewhat small). I've had this router for a few days and have not disconnected once and the speeds are rock solid. My Foscam IP cameras run on the 2.4 GHZ band, while everything else (PC, cell phones, laptop), are on the 5 GHZ band. We've tested everything under heavy load (PC downloading a 15 GB game, while laptop streams HD video, while security cams upload videos to the cloud) with zero issues or slowdowns. This is by far the best router I've owned to date.

I would recommend assigning a name to each device and use a sticky post it to label each device so you can install them at the correct location. title: Nice Dash Camera
text:
The Hyperion auto dash camera is a decent dash cam for the money. It is easy to install and the suction cup holder is very secure. You can choose three different video resolutions; 1296P, 1080P, or 720P. The higher the resolution the shorter the recording duration before the video starts loop recording. You can increase memory by inserting a higher capacity memory card, it comes with a 16GB memory card installed already and it can take a 32GB or up to a 64GB memory card. The recording modes/video files are, Crash detected, Loop-recording, Parking and Photo. You can plug your camera to you computer with the supplied cable to transfer the videos or you can pop out the memory card and put it in a card reader on your computer to transfer the videos. You can also update the camera the same way, if there is an update to the camera.

The camera has other functions as well, it has Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS), Front Collision Warning System, Front Vehicle Departure Warning. They seem to work, but I wouldn't rely on it. It just give beeping tones and sometimes it seems random whey they go off, also if you pass other drivers or vice versa it beeps as well. The good thing is in the menu settings, you can disable the alarms and it doesn't affect the camera recording.

Installation is pretty simple, it comes with a long power cord that can be easily concealed under the trim. The only thing that might be a problem is you need to plug it into the cigarette lighter, so if you don't have another lighter plug outlet, you would have to unplug the camera to for example plug in a cellphone charger. The camera does have a rechargeable battery built in so it can run on battery power for a while, but you have to have the camera plugged in for a while to charge the battery first.

Overall, this is a nice camera and I am very happy with it.

title: I really want to like these...
text:
This is my first purchase of earbuds in the over $200 category. I got the Jabra Elite 65t as soon as they came out and have since bought a couple of other pairs of earbuds in the under $100 category that had better features like IPX7 or 8hr battery life. Therefore I was excited to upgrade to the XM4 for their bettery life and the noise canceling.

Unfortunately, I've had several issues with these. I don't have particularly small ears. Usually the medium tips fit without issue. On the XM4, I started with the medium tips and tested their air tightness using the app. The small tips don't have any kind of seal on my ears without really shoving them super far down my ear canal, so I decided to stick with the medium size. Unfortunately, I have experienced significant ear fatigue enough so that I can't wear the earbuds for more than a couple of hours. I have since switched to the small tips for the sake of comfort, but that means sacrificing any passive noise canceling - and unless I have a defective unit, without the passive noise canceling in addition to the active noise canceling, there is absolutely no difference between having the noise canceling on and off. To me, this completely defeats the purpose of buying noise canceling earbuds.

I also have had issues with connectivity such as the bluetooth connection on my phone suddenly dropping and having to go into the app to manually pair them again.

In terms of battery life, depending on the control settings of each earbud, there can be a difference in the drain of battery between the left and right side. On a bad day, I had a 30% difference with the right draining significantly faster. My earbuds are using the factory settings with the playback controls on the right and the noise canceling on the left for reference.

Both the connectivity problems and the bettery difference between the earbuds has seemed to have gotten better since performing a factory reset, but be aware that there is still a little difference in the rate of battery drain between the L and R earbuds (It's not super significant now and maybe reaches under 7-8% difference at the end of the day).

I bought some Comply foam tips, which I hope will fix the discomfort issue and make the noise canceling work at the optimal rate without the ear fatigue. However, I shouldn't have to modify almost $300 earbuds to make them work like they should. It would help if Sony would offer more sizes of ear tips to help make them more usable for a wider population. Then again, if I have gripes like these, then maybe the XM4s aren't for me. Makes me super sad considering I think that they're probably fantastic for most people.

title: Good and bad - clickers malfunctioned prematurely on two units - the bad is long term reliability (not recommended anymore).
text:
I'm changing my review on this (the original review found below).
I've owned three of these. Two of these mice developed several bad switches by a year's use (the third Evoluent mouse was a Bluetooth mouse and too erratic in behavior to use or talk about here). This failure applies to any of the six mechanical switches within this mouse.

Anyhow, the shape and potential of this mouse is high grade, BUT when the switches (where you click the mouse) go bad, they create instantaneous "multiple, rapid-fire clicks". You'll find yourself accidentally deleting pages, or backing up multiple internet pages, or collapsing/minimizing pages you didn't want to, etc. The behavior is unpredictable and makes the mouse useless.
SO, IN SPITE OF THIS MOUSES ADVANTAGES, UNRELIABILITY IS THE GAMECHANGER.

I've used just about 5 ergo styled mouses over the last 15 years - mainly all of them in a technical graphic oriented environments or at home where the ergonomics are mediocre (if you are up on ergonomics). This particular mouse takes about a month to get used to, but as you get accustomed to it, you may find yourself hooked. I too learned to use both left and right hand mouses to relieve pain, but since adopting this mouse over the couple years I've been using it, I've not had to resort to shifting to right then left hand usage.
You can program this thing to make any key do any function - you can place the right click at your thumb for example or turn off a click position altogether. The hand positioning is going to do you good if you have any hand pain at all.
The wireless version works fine (just turn it off to save the battery of course). The bluetooth version is very undependable; I do hear they have made improvements, my old bluetooth would jump all around the screen at times, but my new one was DOA, so I went back to the wireless version which I've used for about a year now without trouble.
Its good mouse. They really should drop the price point down to about $80 after all this time, but despite that, I'd say give this mouse your consideration.

If this device was HDCP compatible, I would expect it to output sound through the HDMI connection to any compatible device, including my plasma TV.

Before getting this switcher, I ran my DVR with HDMI out to the TV - video and sound,- no problem. After putting the device in line between the DVR and the TV, HDMI sound no longer goes through. So I believe the problem is in this device.

Correction: I later discovered that if you change the switcher from one source to any other then back again, it "finds" the sound. Many times, I turned on the TV and the DVR and got no sound. As a person who tutors people who are not technologically savvy, I am going to review this tablet from the point of view of someone who has not had one before and whether or not this is a good choice if you want to get one.

I have been told by several business people and those who claim to be very tech savvy that they have gotten rid of their laptops except for occasional spreadsheet work in their offices or at home. Can you get rid of your laptop by getting a tablet like this? Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS TABLET LIKE?
SIDE SWITCHES
This tablet is around the size of an ipad mini or a Kindle. The on off switch is on the upper right hand side (with screen facing you) and below it is a rocker switch just below the power switch. There is a space between the two buttons which will allow for elastic bands should you want to get a case for it that has them. That will make it so that the tablet will not be turned on and off by accident. The power button has to be pushed and held for a moment before the unit turns on.

SCREEN
The tablet screen is shiny which can be annoying, but that is the nature of the beast.
The touch sensitivity is excellent- I did not find any problems with response time or lag.
The orientation changing when you turn the screen around is also well set. It works nicely and is not overly sensitive.

INPUT
To input into the tablet, you have a choice to either type or speak what you want the tablet to do. I have to say that this tablet responds very well to either set of input. After working with several i-pads, my daughter constantly raves about how this Acer tablet is superior in the way it responds to input with the microphone than the i-pads are. I have not had any problem with typing into this tablet beyond what I normally do on any unit. The microphone occasionally mistypes a word, but it is not nearly as bad as I expected it to.

Response time of the tablet is excellent. I am quite impressed with how quickly it responds to input without lag or difficulty.

APPS
I have put a few apps on this unit which tend to be popular with tablet users. Sketchbook Pro is one of those apps. I really like it. The response time is good, and the app seems to work well on this tablet. I also love the radio app which allows you to listen to radio stations in the area or around the country. With a case that folds into a stand, it is a great panel to use in a room where you want to listen to the radio.

Quite a few apps that come in the tablet already are handy and easy to use. The screen is quite intuitive and easy to use.

INTERNET USAGE
This tablet is wi-fi accessible to the internet which means that you can not go out in no-man's land to use it like you can an android phone, but you have to be near a wi-fi station to use it.

The wi-fi response time is excellent- although it does occasionally lag when the signals get weak- something that all wi-fi units will do.

Android is a Google engine so everything you do will be monitored by Google or you will be using something they have designed to get where you want to go. You can find other ways to purchase apps if you don't like the Google store, however, such as Amazon.

This tablet comes with McAfee virus scan which is not a huge deal, but I am not sure how to replace that yet, should I desire to do so.

CAMERA
I am not a big advocate of phone and tablet cameras. This one has a decent camera to use on the back, and an adequate camera on the front of the camera to use for Skype which is pretty much all you need. If you want a really nice camera, buy one. For quick pictures to capture something you want to show someone, then this will be fine.

PROS
Easy to hold
Screen responsive
Speech recognition works well
Good fast performance
Boots up quickly
Clear screen makes reading books nice
Good colors for photos on the screen (better than laptops)
Power button hard to accidentally turn on or off
Learning is pretty intuitive for first time users

CONS
Wi-fi only
Not as easy to use as laptop for extensive typing
Can be a bit clumsy to use at times (the nature of tablets)
Start up literature is a bit underwhelming for first time users

THE BOTTOM LINE

CAN YOU GET RID OF YOUR LAPTOP?
Can you get rid of your laptop to substitute this tablet? My answer would be no.

Even if all you did was go on the internet to wander through web sites, using a tablet is a bit cumbersome if you want to do any kind of extensive writing. If you use the microphone, it will probably be pretty accurate, but you will still have to use the keyboard to correct what is used.

For occasional internet usage, watching videos, movies, and reading books, this tablet is fabulous. I think it works beautifully. I would say that it is just as nice as other more expensive tablets and you will invest a lot less money in it.

If you want a tablet and do not want to pay a fortune for it, this is the way to go. The Acer Iconia A1-830 is an excellent value and I use mine a lot. I just could not substitute it completely for my laptop. I prefer to have a choice in my browser, features, and fine tuning or replacement of parts should I desire to do so.

I do find that having the tablet helps a lot when I want to quickly do something on the internet and don't want to boot up my laptop. This tablet is pretty quick and I like it. If you are a tech fanatic and have to have the biggest and best, you might find fault with this tablet, however. It is worth a test run in any case.

UPDATE 3/4/2015 SAMSUNG GALAXY 4 (8 inch) vs ACER ICONIA A1-830
I have had quite a chance to get to know this tablet over time and also to use a Samsung Galaxy 4 8 inch tablet in comparison both on its own and with a keyboard. After working with both tablets, I have to say that I still prefer the Acer over the Samsung and here is why:

-Acer has slightly smaller screen area, but is easier to work on
-Acer has the return and menu buttons incorporated into the screen instead of on the side so it rotates with screen
-Acer surface is less shiny and has less glare
-Performance of Acer is the same as the Samsung in terms of speed
-Wifi of Acer is as good as the Samsung
-keyboard of Acer is much easier to use than Samsung (the one in the screen)
-set up of the Acer is much easier and user friendly
-voice commands on Acer works MUCH better than on the Samsung
-Samsung speaker is a bit nicer than Acer, but I use a bluetooth speaker for best sound anyway.
-Samsung battery does last a bit longer than the Acer, but the frustrations of the Samsung still make me prefer the Acer.

All in all, I have to say that I have tried to honestly look at both tablets and give them a fair comparison and I still like the Acer better. The price is better and the ease of use is better too. The microphone on the Acer seems much more responsive than the Samsung. The screen of the Samsung is a bit more dense in terms of pixels and color perhaps, but the glare is more annoying. I also get very irritated at the side buttons on the Samsung. They are static (stay put) and when the tablet is on its side, it is way too easy to hit a button that screws up what I am trying to do on the Samsung. This is especially true when I am trying to type something and is VERY frustrating.

There is one thing about the Samsung that I really wish the Acer had and that is longer battery time. The Samsung does run a little longer than the Acer without having to recharge. The speaker on the Samsung is a bit nicer, but with my portable bluetooth speaker as my main source of listening, I don't find that to be a problem for me.

So, after time and the chance to use the Acer and the Samsung so I could compare them, I still really like the Acer tablet better. Because I do a lot of graphics work and computer work, I still would not get rid of my laptop or desktop, but I do save a lot of time using this tablet when I want to look up quick information and cruise the internet.

UPDATE March 2016
I wanted to take a moment to update you concerning this device.

As time has gone on I have enjoyed using the Acer Iconia A1-830 very much. It is a nice tablet for an affordable price.

HAVE I HAD PROBLEMS?
A few.
-tablet went nuts as if a baby were in charge of it and had five Redbull drinks first. I rebooted and cleared out some programs and all was fine.

-I could not move my information from my device to my PC- this was solved, but it has taken a lot of research, effort and time. The support at the Acer site is rather pitiful to be honest. That is one thing that I will say about this, is compared to Samsung, Acer does not support their devices as well as they should, but then again, the price is a lot less too.

IS THIS STILL WORKING?
Yes., I use it daily and it still is working. I keep the HD less than 60% full as I do with most devices as they tend to work best that way. I find that it connects via wi-fi at times when other devices in the house do not. I also find that the battery wears down a lot less quickly if I turn off location and even wi-fi if I don't need it.

NO UPGRADE PAST KIT-KAT 4.4.2
There will be no upgrades to Lollipop or beyond, so if you want a more modern unit, then try for something new.

MY REVIEW STANDS
I now have a Samsung Galaxy Tab S2 that I am using and it of course passes the Acer by a mile, but then again, it is a much more expensive machine too.

title: Highly Functional Quality Product. Near perfect!
text:
This keyboard is great. It is comfortable and the keys have nice tactile feedback. Overall I would highly recommend this keyboard to anyone.

I will list a few pros and cons.
Pro:
Highly functional: There are 7 keys with icons for their default function (IE: webcam button, Calendar button) but these can be changed to whatever function you want. Additionally, there are 12 Function keys ( accessed with an Fn Key + F# key) These also can be reassigned to your desired function. This includes; open a web page, keystroke, open an app, open a file or a folder. ( 2 function keys are dedicated to the battery status and eject button and can not be overwritten)

Gamers: Keyboard software permits you to disable a few keys, including the Windows key! (Disable: Caps Lock, Windows Key, Scroll lock, Num lock and Insert)

Sleep Key. Need to step away from your work. There is a dedicated sleep key. One press. (does not wake it up)

It's ergonomic! It is very comfortable to type on this keyboard. It did not however improve my typing speed.

Plug and play. (Note: you must download Logitech's setpoint software for advanced settings) but if you like the keyboard's functions as they are there is no installation required.

1 USB port to rule them all! Logitech Unify USB software allows you to pair up to 6 wireless devices to the USB receiver. Meaning you only have to use 1 USB port if you have other Logitech devices such as a mouse. (Keyboard is also offered in a bundle)

Included wristguard! (non-removable)

Texture. The way things feel is very important to me. The wrist guard has a nice soft leather feel kin to a nice steering wheel cover. The keys have light texturing to them also. The various buttons are a smooth texture. The use of various textures on the keyboard really makes it look premium also.

Media Controls: Play/Pause/Stop/Volume

Cons:

Key sound: The keys have a very plastic clack to them with no clicky. This is obviously not a mechanical keyboard but there is a noticeably hollow, loose, plastic cheap-sounding noise to this keyboard. This is not a deal-breaker. It is quiet enough that it is not disruptive to the office or sleeping partner.

Size: This is not a compact keyboard by any means. The wristguard is not removable. (19x10 inches)

Not backlit: This keyboard obviously is not RGB or backlit but it is worth mentioning. If your intended use is in low light or no light this is not ideal.

Key spacing: As this is designed to be ergonomic and maximize comfort it is clearly designed with intent. However, transitioning from my work dell keyboard with very tight key spacing and the same with my laptop keyboard there is an adjustment required. Since it is designed so that each key is where your fingers naturally rest you will quickly adapt.

title: What Happens When Things Go Wrong...
text:
When I first purchased my 3 TB MBL some time ago I was quite pleased. Network access, remote access, even an android app. In short, everything my DLink had plus the app and a nicer look on the shelf. I used it extensively for pulling up photos on my cell phone when I was bored as well as to store my most important files. I didn't back them up, a back-up drive is something I kept saying I would add later...

14 months later (note the 12 month warranty had just expired) the drive stopped being accessible over the network. I spent a week and at least 40 hours of my time going back and forth with tech support by e-mail and trying every option they could offer, and the result was that they deemed the unit broken. They said that the unit can not be opened because that would break the drive inside, and they said that they can't fix it. They "kindly" offered me a referral to one of several companies that give them a kick back for data recovery services. Incidentally, I asked two for pricing by e-mail and they didn't respond.

So I took the unit apart and bought a new unit and took that one apart and swapped the drives. Neither one worked. After talking to support again it turns out that WD didn't want these to be upgradable because if they were upgradable you could buy a cheap drive instead of a new unit so they code each board to the drive that will be in it. TO make matters worse, they encoded the drive in a Linux format that no known version of Linux can translate. Attaching it to my Linux system I couldn't mount it using any utility. Several Linux recovery programs couldn't do anything either.

Okay, having told you why I will never buy a WD NAS again, I should now tell you how to fix this if you have the same problem that I do: DiskInternals makes a program called Linux Reader. That's right, Linux can't read the drive but a program designed to read Linux drives from within Windows can! Recovering the data to a drive is time consuming though. I tried it all at once but that froze after a few days. Then I tried one major directory at a time and that worked better. But recovering nearly 3 TB of data has taken a very long time! I'm about 3 MONTHS into the recovery effort and I have about 400 GB remaining. After starting on my wife's computer because mine is a laptop and causing a few crashes and a lot of delays I finally had to pull out an older computer and set it up just to run this program.

If anyone has the same problem and can't get this solution to work, I'll do my best to help if you simply reply to this review and give me all the details. If anyone is considering buying a WD NAS, I want to encourage you to buy a DLink model 323 (I think the 325 is the current version but it is missing some features so I'd get an older one) instead. I've had that thing running for 5 years without a glitch!

title: Trick to get it to work with a docking computer
text:
This works as advertised but is a bit expensive so I give it 4 stars. I'm writing this review to share a trick I figured out with my docked computer...

When a docked computer powers up to 100% the charger shuts off, resulting in the peripherals shutting down if the computer charger is set to be the "master" power source. The trick is to set the monitor to be the "master" power source, then go into control panel so the monitor doesn't shut off for an hour or two when the computer is plugged in. You can then hook everything else up to be a slave unit, including the computer charger itself. This solution is working great for me- powering down my subwoofer, speakers, scanner, laptop charger, and desk lamp...

title: Really great laptop
text:
HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 ssd

Now that I have used a touch screen laptop I can never go back. This is something I didn't know I needed, but now that I have it, it's something I can't live without. The response of the screen is great and I don't notice any lag. I don't flip the screen around to use it like a tablet very often, but it's nice to have the option to do so.

For the PC, it's 128gb ssd is fast. Windows startup and applications load quickly. The 8gb of ram help the applications feel snappy and is sufficient for doing day to day work. This is not a gaming laptop by any means, but does feel quite powerful. It doesn't have a dedicated GPU and uses the 8th gen I5 to host the graphics. That being said the 8th gen I5 is no slouch. It turbos up to 3.9 ghz and has 4 cores, so you should be plowing through most tasks with ease. The additional 1tb hard drive helps a lot because the 128gb ssd just isn't enough in 2019.

The size and weight of the laptop is well balanced and has a very high quality feel. The battery life is great and I have gone all day with out having to plug it in. Obviously, you mileage may very depending on how hard you are working the system. The keyboard and the track pad have a very responsive feel. It has a fingerprint reader on the side for easy login which is a great feature

I wish they ditched the 1tb spinning drive and just put in a 1tb ssd. I also wish it had 16gb of ram or the option to add more later. For the price, this laptop is pretty great. I wouldn't nock off any stars for those two points. Having a 1tb ssd and 16gb of ram would put this over $1000 and probably not necessary for most people. Overall, best laptop I've owned hands down.

title: Perfect fit!
text:
I just got a new plum colored Kindle Paperwhite and after looking through tons of case options, I ultimately decided to go with the case that matched my device. I was concerned about it fitting because there are so many conflicting views on this subject, but I figured their returns are so easy I might as well just try it out for myself. I’m glad I did.

When you close the cover it sticks to it on the far right side with a magnet and puts the screen to sleep. Then when you reopen it the screen lights up and you slide it awake. So simplistic and exactly what I hoped for. I love that when you flip the front cover back it lays almost flush (see picture) and magnetizes to that too eliminating the issue of it flapping around while you’re reading (an issue I constantly had with my older Nook cover). It’s also a sort of suede like material on the inner cover so it feels easier to hold it. Improves your grip on the device. The outside of the cover is also very nicely made. It’s slim so it doesn’t add any unnecessary bulk or weight to the Kindle and just looks very sleek. I’m impressed with it and glad I took a chance. The plum color of the Kindle and this case are so pretty. I thought it’d be too pink, but it’s definitely more mauve. Love it.

title: Buy this
text:
Software Features:
This AGPtEK mp3 player is a really good alternative to an ipod or zune which is more expensive and offers less storage space while offering the opportunity to drag and drop files into the mp3 player folder directly, once it's connected via usb cable to your computer. This feature is important to me, because not all my music is properly tagged, so music organizing software like itunes doesn't recognise the files. This is no problem with the AGPtEK mp3 player, since I can always manually find the file and drop it in.
Hardware Features: The build is attractive and sturdy. I appreciate the glass display and nice solid but light aluminum casing. The shape is a basic rectangle which works fine for me since I like a minimalist look. One thing I don't like about the build is that the click wheel click very loudly and is a little stiff, which is a hassle to use when you're trying to scroll down your music list.The wheel feels a little cheap, its quality is not on par with the rest of the build. The screen is not as large as a typical ipod's but is sufficient. The title of your song will have to scroll a bit to be read fully, which can be kind annoying. ANother great thing is that you can upgrade storage using a micro SD chip which means you're quadrupling your storage. score!

Music Playback features: They have a nice EQ option if you're into that. The fast forward is really slow. The mp3 player plays a bunch of different formats like mp3, oog, wav, flac, etc... You can also store audiobooks, videos, photos, and record sound. I havn't use these features yet.

Accessories: The arm band is a nice bonus. It fits perfectly and leaves holes for charging and headphones. It holds the mp3 player snuggly. The band is smooth and not scratchy. If you have small arms the band can be pretty big, it's adjustable but there will be somg extra band hanging around. t is fastened by velcro.
The headphones are like $10 quality. They're not bad, but they're not audiophile. They don't fit very well as I have small ears but they'll do in a pinch.

Charging: There is an option to charge and transfer or charge and play music once you connect the player to your computer. CHarging it fully takes about 1-2 hours. The mp3's battery is very good, I haven't been able to drain the battery completely, but keeping it off, it's been able to stay charged for over 3 days.

title: If you want the whole surface covered, you don't want this.
text:
Okay, so, I successfully installed the screen protector in accordance with the instructions. There was exactly enough application solution for my inner perfectionist to place and replace the protector 3 times. As an added precaution - both because the device was dirty and I live in a dusty house full of cat, dog and people hair - I cleaned it with some glass cleaner, dabbed it with a paper towel, then polished it with a soft cloth, and then a lint free cloth to get off any lint from the soft cloth - so, yes, if you work at it, you can get this protector on with ZERO lint/particles underneath it. I've done it and it is glorious.

Why the 3 stars then, you ask? Well, as I do intend to own this product for some time, I am more than a little upset that the screen protector is not sized to completely cover the screen side of this device. If centered, there is about 1/8 of an inch of uncovered surface on either edge. This is going to cause uneven wear and eventually a ring of uncovered surface around the covered. This bothers me because this item is specifically advertised as fitting the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 and it doesn't. It almost fits. So, it's almost doing its job.

Aside from that it is crystal clear, easy to install, easy to remove, doesn't appear to leave any residue - all the things one desires in a screen protector, so if you don't mind that your device will have a ring of uneven use around the edge, go for it.

title: Nice mix of ambiance and sound quality
text: I was unsure of what to make of this when I first saw it. It’s interesting and unique for sure, but what is the point really? After using it for a couple weeks now I get it. It’s a modern way of adding ambiance and beautiful sound quality to any environment. I worried that it would be fragile. I’m sure it would break if dropped or banged against something, it is glass after all,  if it’s surprisingly sturdy and feels durable. I’m careful when I carry it from room to room, and would definitely travel with it in the box it arrived in, but I don’t find myself cradling it like an egg. It’s more like carrying a heavy candlestick. And it does light up just like one. I thought that might be a gimmicky feature but it’s actually really cool. You can set it to flicker like a flame by holding in the power button. Don’t release it or you’ll just turn it off. The brightness is adjustable via the buttons on the base. It’s not going to replace a lamp but it’s nice for an intimate dinner or in addition to candles. I really appreciated it when our power went out one night. It gave us some illumination and some music to break the silence. The sound quality is gorgeous. The mid and high tones are beautiful and perfect. The bass is nice. It’s not going to vibrate your walls but this speaker isn’t designed for that. It’s meant to set a nice atmosphere and it does so remarkably well. The one downside is the price tag. Not that it isn’t necessarily deserving of it but I feel that it could be a bit of an extravagance for a lot of people. I think if price isn’t a concern and you’re looking for something a bit nicer than your basic Bluetooth speaker you would definitely enjoy and appreciate this item. I’m happy to have it in my home and love the warmth and beauty it brings.

title: Decent for media consumption; buy it while it's on sale
text:
TL;DR

The Kindle Fire HD 8 is a serviceable tablet if you don’t intend to use it for much outside of consuming media, primarily from Amazon’s in-house apps. If you’re interested, I recommend that you wait until they’re on sale before making the purchase.

Full Review:

I bought my Kindle Fire HD 8 primarily for listening to music. I use Amazon Music (Unlimited subscriber) and it has a headphone jack. Not wanting to deal with the ads from the lockscreen, I paid to have them removed. Over the past few weeks, I’ve been playing around with the device to see what it’s capable of when it comes to media consumption. Here’s what I’ve come up with! I did manage to sideload Google Play and several apps. I’ll reflect on those experiences, though any issues I had from this will not count against the device, as Google Play and the apps from it are not officially supported.

Interface and Build Quality
You are pretty much stuck with their stock interface. You can’t remove ANY of the Amazon apps from the homescreen. However, you can hide them away in a folder. This cleaned things up, nicely. Toward the top of the screen, you have a static bar that shows your last 2 apps, as well as some recommended apps. They do manage to sneak a sponsored app in there from time to time. Seeing that I paid to get rid of ads, this annoyed me (though it really doesn’t impact my use.) I actually like typing on this more than I do my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6 Lite or my Samsung S22 phone, which surprised me. One would think they’d make sure their own apps are working on their own devices at least as well as the apps work on their competitors devices.

The tablet itself feels kinda cheap, but not as cheap as I expected. The screen’s glass isn’t as smooth as my Samsung devices, but it’s quite functional. You can tell there’s not much power under the hood, as apps take a few seconds to load, and there’s sometimes interface lag when interacting with them. The onboard speakers suck, but I don’t use them. Headphones are the way to go… and since it has a headphone jack, I’m all set. The display is plenty for what I use it for.

Support
I’ve reached out to Amazon a few times to ask questions, or to get help. They’ve been incredibly responsive. The reps have always been courteous and informative. High marks here!

Audio and Video Quality
Music sounds great through my Audio Technica ATH-M50x headphones, especially HD and Ultra HD from Amazon Music. Strangely, the app does not have an EQ option (I can adjust the EQ on my Windows PC and on my other Android devices.) It supports my Fosi Audio DS1 with no problems. This improves the sound a bit (mostly making things a bit louder.) It did not power up my Fosi Audio K5 Pro, however. Unfortunately, the Kindle Fire HD 8 did not support my Bluetooth Audio Technica ATH-SR50BT’s, which was a disappointment. On the flipside, I was able to sideload 4Stream and the Andover Songbird app to get it to stream HD audio to my Denon D-M41, which was a pleasant surprise.

I took some time to watch some streaming video via Prime Video, Netflix and YouTube (sideloaded via Google Play.) Even though it’s not a true “HD” display, the screen is small enough to make it not matter so much. Lord of the Rings - Fellowship of the Rings probably benefited from this, as the movie didn’t age well in our HD world. The audio on it was also quite engaging through my headphones. Ash vs the Evil Dead on Netflix also streamed flawlessly, and looked great on the screen. YouTube videos play just fine as well, even though the app was sideloaded.

As an eReader
The Kindle Fire HD 8 works great as an eReader, as one would expect. Since I don’t plan to read much from it, I didn’t explore it much. Books loaded just fine, and you can interact with them as you’d expect (the Kindle is pretty robust for this, for those who’re interested.)

Non-media Consumption
I tried getting Discord to work on the Fire HD 8. While I was able to install it, the experience was pretty terrible. Browsing the internet with the Silk browser leaves some to be desired, and the mail/calendar apps are not something I’m interested in using. Again, I’m using this primarily for music, so I’m fine with this. However, if I needed to use it for anything productive, I’d be quite frustrated.

Google Play
Instructions on how to get Google Play installed are readily available online, and it’s easily doable within an hour’s time. I was able to install an EQ for my music, which works okay (I did have the app crash once.) The Gmail app loaded fairly well, as did Google Chrome. However, I can’t sync Chrome, as my email account was already used to activate the Kindle. There haven’t been any issues with YouTube. Dragon Quest 1 and 2 installed flawlessly and seem to work fine. However, Baldur’s Gate 1 & 2, along with other Beamdog games did not install at all (these aren’t officially supported, but folks claim it works. Not for me!) Again, none of these experiences with Google Play will count for or against my overall rating for this device. I’m simply stating them in case anyone else is interested in tinkering.

Ultimately, the Kindle Fire HD 8 is okay for the money (when on sale.) It works for my purposes, but I can tell it’d leave a lot to be desired if I wanted to use it for anything more. The fact that they still advertise apps on the home screen, even after you pay to remove ads is annoying (enough to knock my rating down a star.) I do suspect that the Kindle Fire devices are probably loss-leaders, and any ads they can cram in help generate income.

title: Perhaps some firmware updates could save it
text:
I was excited to set up my new router, replacing an already solid [[ASIN:B002HWRJY4 NETGEAR Wireless Router - N600 Dual Band Gigabit (WNDR3700)]]. After a relatively easy basic setup and a more lengthy configuration to my specific needs (setting up specific IP addresses for devices, port forwarding, and USB shares) I really got down to using it. It worked well enough, but 5ghz range was dubious and easily thwarted by even minor obstacles. Running some analytics on my tablet, I saw that the 5gz signal never really separated from other relatively strong signals (coming from my [[ASIN:B006W41W4Q Turtle Beach Ear Force XP400 Dolby Surround Sound Gaming Headset]]). Whatever logic used by the router to automatically select channels is simply lazy or non-functional. Manually selecting a better channel helped a bit, but the overall issues remain. On the plus side, speed with a strong signal is very good, and the ethernet seems up to gigabit specs (100GB+ transfers are as fast as with other gigabit routers and switches). Additionally streaming media never studders (the reason is less than ideal as you'll see in the next paragraph). All in all this is a 4 star router, with one huge fault that changes my opinion.

The firmware is very raw. First off it's advanced functions (part of why you buy a $100+ router or really any new one these days) are either hard to access, oddly confusing by trying to be easy (work different than most routers), or non-existent (which can take some time to figure out due to the first two issues). My biggest beef is that QOS is broken. Torrents never get more than 1.5-5kps using default settings--even if no other traffic is present. There is no specific rule that does this, as it's just on behind the scenes when QOS is enabled (by default). Typically their is a rule you can modify, and no matter what, low priority traffic always flows freely when there is nothing else going on. Alas I have no choice but to disable QOS, which frankly is a needed feature when downloading torrents and a reason for using an advanced router. Lastly USB drives are pushed hard to the point where their temps are damaging. My old router and my [[ASIN:B0064XAJ5I Western Digital My Book Live Duo 4 TB Personal Cloud Storage Drive]] never cause their USB drives to behave this way in a similar usage scenario. I imagine it would be easy enough to fix these issues along with enhancing the automatic channel selection with a firmware update. The wireless performance may still be less than ideal, but it would definitely be a solid choice.

Until these updates are made, there probably are better solutions, especially if you are looking to use advanced features.

Pros
* simple non-intimidating interface
* good, though not great performance
* great feature list
* potential to be even better with updates

Cons
* advanced features hard to access or use (in some cases missing)
* broken QOS
* USB drives run real hot
* real world performance

But this extra area allows you to include a foam shock absorber above and below the drive. I recommend white polyethylene foam, not the gray polyurethane. The softer gray foam will last only ten years before breaking down and reverting to its natural sticky glue-like liquid form. Very messy and destructive. Polyethylene foam lasts forever. You can also put the drive in its anti-static bag. That alone stops the drive from moving about inside the case.

text:

If you don't have a USB to eithernet adapter you'll need a USB flash drive and another computer to get the updated drivers to this system.

title: This thing really packs a punch!
text:
I ordered the 'Divoom Pro Premium 40W 12Hour Playtime TWS Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Water Resistant for Indoor/Outdoor Use(Black)' for review.

I am a sucker for portable Bluetooth speakers and I had to give this one a go and I must say that I was not disappointed (well maybe just a little - continue reading .....). My first impression when opening the box was that this thing is heavy for how small it is. The speaker itself is a nice size with a beautiful basic design. The controls are really simple and feel very tactile. They are easy to feel which button you are pressing. The speaker comes with really nice braided type cables. One for charging and one Aux cable. Both are quite short however which really isn't a big deal. Especially for the fact that once you fully charge this beast, it'll give you a "claimed" 12 hour play time. I have not pushed this limit yet as I have only used it for a couple hours at a time but I have not recharged it yet. Although this speaker has a water resistant rating of IPX5, I have not tested this, but from how this is built, I would feel confident that I could take it outside and not worry about a little Oregon rain or being splashed on by the kids playing in the sprinklers. The really cool thing about this speaker is that you can charge your device while listening to it via the USB type A port.

There are only a couple of cons with this speaker in my opinion. First con - Where is the USB C charging? I always have to point this out with new products. This charges via Micro USB. USB C should be integrated and standard in all new products in my opinion. Second con is that when watching videos there are sync issues. So if you are planning to use this for watching anything video streaming, it gets pretty annoying. This is a new product, and I would think that both USB C and Bluetooth 5.0 should be a standard these days. With that said my overall impression with this Divoom speaker, is that for listening to music it's a beast. It pairs up easily with not much of a delay at all once it has been initially paired to your device. Turn the power on and it'll pair back up fast and ready to play. I also like the fact that if you have two of these (I wish I did) they can sync together to produce a much fuller stereo experience. Maybe down the road I will get a second one and update this review with how well that feature works. I hope that this was helpful!

title: Steps lively for multi-tasking, responsive touchscreen, DVD RW drive, awesome battery ** APRIL 2016 UPDATE ***
text:
I've been using a 2009 17.9" Gateway Windows 7 laptop happily all these years until just recently when it began to cough and sputter and generally show signs of wanting to die. I nursed it for several months while shopping for a replacement and suddenly this Toshiba L55T-C/5388 appeared from Vine. Serendipity. I am writing my review from the Toshiba actually rather than my tablet which what I've had to resort to for the past few months - that's a nice change actually. My initial impressions after a week of daily use are pretty good overall with some niggling design complaints for the physical hardware.First - for the record ... I'm not a gamer - just a regular person using my laptop to write articles for the local newspaper now and then, do a lot of email, a lot of online shopping, some social media stuff, watch some videos now and then, sort and store serious quantities of photos and average net surfing. If I want to listen to music, I tend to use Alexa (the Echo) for that rather than my computer and we watch movies on the big television around here - though sometimes I'll use my laptop instead of my tablet for tv shows etc when I'm traveling.

This Toshiba has a very nice high definition screen and I haven't noticed any fuzziness or blurred screen edges etc. The HD video I downloaded from Amazon as a test sample looked as crisp and bright on the laptop as it did on our Samsung 1080p television. The sound clarity is very good for dialogue and background music - the full speaker running across the length of the front of the machine is really good and the volume is quite loud.
Additionally, the touchscreen is responsive, but not so sensitive that just brushing it will mess your page up or close an open tab. I did run into a couple of sessions where the screen would go to black as I was scrolling rapidly by touch - this seems to be a Windows 10 issue when using the new Edge browser and not a laptop physical issue. I haven't had a repeat of this in the Chrome Browser in a week. (It could also have been a fluke)

The battery life on this computer is freaking amazing! I've been using it for almost 3 hours now for a variety of things and it's currently sitting at 74% with an estimated 6 hours and 35 minutes run time left. By three hours of use, my Gateway would have already been at 10% and that's before it started having problems. Thus far, I have used this laptop for a five hour straight run - writing, with email refreshing in the background and music playing as a test at the same time and the battery barely hit 52% when I was finished working.

Uploading and transferring files from both the cloud and my old computer hasn't been as big a hassle as I expected. The USB 2.0 thumb drive I had handy worked just fine and everything came over intact. The cloud transfer was a bit stickier just because Windows 10 now wants to make unzipping files more complicated than before. (Thanks Microsoft) Additionally, the DVD RW drive works fine and I have had no problems at all uploading the software for my 3D printer and downloading files from the net for it. For those that are interested, unlike other reviewers, I had zero problems uploading and am now using Google Chrome as my browser etc. I've included a photo of my basic screen - the Chrome icon is right there. You just have download Chrome and then unzip it manually.

My one star deduction is for physical comfort. This is a light computer compared to my previous one and I appreciate that. However, the edges are not rounded off. They are sharp, square and pointy. This means that as you are typing - doesn't matter if it's on your lap or a desk - after awhile, these pointy bits will dig into your wrists or arms and this HURTS. My five hour marathon the other day left a little indention on my right wrist. That is just ridiculous. The second design flaw is the touch pad. It is very large and sits perfectly flush with the base of the laptop. This is pretty, but you tend to brush over it as you are actually typing and that can make the cursor jump - now you're typing in an entirely new location. These two issues are obnoxious enough that I am now looking for a way to create a little rubber bumper for the front edge of the computer and a wireless mouse.

In general, this is a nice replacement for my old workhorse Gateway - I've grown used to the smaller screen because Toshiba has made it very easy to enlarge the font and any image on this screen. The 8 gig of ram makes multi tasking and switching from things prompt and thus far, I haven't experienced any lagginess. There is some bloatware pre-installed (like with any computer), but it is easy to get rid of. WIndows 10 requires a learning curve of course, but that's not the laptop's fault. Four solid stars after almost ten days and if that changes, I'll update.

*********SIX MONTH UPDATE April 29, 2016 ********

After a little over six full months of regular, almost daily use, I have had no problems at all with this laptop. It just does its job with no drama. It streams movies, music and uploads photos and files to the cloud. It handles my word processing needs and email and all the regular stuff anyone does on a computer. It also handles my software for my 3-D printer with grace. I am still very pleased with the battery life and it has had no trouble connecting via blue tooth to my external speakers when needed. I still don't like the slightly sharp edges on the corners, but it's not the end of the world. All in all, this is a nice machine and I'm still using it and pleased with it in general.
